reviews.text:
I recently took my child to the TLADC clinic, and I am extremely satisfied with the experience we had. From the moment we arrived, the staff was welcoming and professional. They made us feel comfortable and assured us that they were there to support us every step of the way.

The evaluation process itself was thorough and comprehensive. The clinicians took the time to get to know my child and to fully understand his strengths and challenges. They used a variety of assessments and techniques to gather a complete picture of his development and functioning.

Overall, I feel that we received an accurate and reliable diagnosis at this clinic. The clinicians were compassionate and understanding, and they provided us with valuable resources and recommendations for next steps. I would highly recommend this clinic to anyone seeking an autism diagnosis for their child.

The service provided by TLADC was all that I was hoping for - efficient, thorough, friendly and informative.

There were no surprises and, from start to finish, the process and inputs were very clearly set out. All the questions I had were answered. I thoroughly appreciated being able to discuss my child as an individual and felt that everything I said I was listened to and taken into account.
The process also served as a perfect gateway to discussing ASD with my child and by the time of the diagnosis, he was very comfortable with it.

The outcome report was also comprehensive and insightful, and included some very clear recommendations for me to take forward with my child’s school.

I’d recommend TLADC to anyone seeking to explore an ASD diagnosis.
Kind, empathetic, and professional in every way.

reviews.text: My wife, with acquired neurodivergence related to PTSD, trusted London Psychiatry Clinic to document her ongoing harms during an extremely sensitive and distressing time when she was experiencing severe symptoms and repeatedly requested documentation. Unfortunately, not only did the clinic completely fail to document these harms, but the doctor also made no notes during the assessment. The assessment letter provided did not meet professional standards and is evidence of the doctor’s complete lack of engagement with my wife’s situation and a total dismissal of the factors contributing to her harm. To make matters worse, the doctor misframed my wife’s legitimate concerns about ongoing harm and harassment by applying discriminatory labeling to her communication style, which is a natural protective response related to her acquired neurodivergence. This perpetuated the very harm she was urgently requesting to be documented. Such mischaracterisation by a healthcare professional not only undermines trust but also constitutes a breach of professional duty and standards of care. The clinic’s failure to maintain contemporaneous clinical notes perpetuated significant harm,  exacerbating her PTSD symptoms and contributing to premature perimenopausal health complications.  PTSD is a serious condition that profoundly affects the neuroendocrine system, altering key hormones such as oxytocin and vasopressin and disrupting the regulation of stress hormones like cortisol. These disruptions can significantly impact physical health, including contributing to premature perimenopausal complications. The clinic’s failure to maintain contemporaneous clinical notes caused significant harm to my wife, who has acquired neurodivergence related to PTSD. PTSD is a serious condition that disrupts hormonal and neurological balance, affecting stress regulation and overall health. However, the doctor disregarded all this and treated my wife’s situation based on his own assumptions and misunderstandings of PTSD rather than accurately documenting what she reported during her assessment. This reveals a profound lack of knowledge and understanding of the condition, leading to substandard care. Despite repeated requests for accurate documentation and reasonable adjustments, her needs remained unmet. The clinic not only failed to provide an acceptable assessment letter but also falsely justified minimal recording as standard practice. This justification is misleading and directly violates professional standards, especially given my wife’s urgent need for accurate documentation. The doctor made no notes, showed zero engagement with my wife’s concerns, and instead provided an irrelevant and inappropriate rant about ChatGPT, which the clinic absurdly calls “standard practice.” Such failures amount to a breach of duty and fall far below the expected standards of care. I advise those seeking mental health care to avoid clinics that lack transparency and rely on misleading language to exploit distressing situations and patient vulnerability. Transparency and honesty are essential for trust and effective care. Based on our experience, this clinic lacks honesty and transparency, using misleading language to justify grave breaches of their duty of care. Such practices obscure the truth and exploit vulnerable patients at their most distressing moments.

We consulted Dr Hayley Ponsford, who is very experienced, a fantastic listener and happy to go the extra mile. We now feel confident that our daughter will receive the help she needs.

reviews.text:
This charity no longer take phone calls or provide a telephone service for people with autism ! They expect autistic people to be able to navigate and get whatever assistance they need on the internet. Completely defeats the object of what autism truly is and the struggles they have! Appalling service! I complained but they did nothing!

All I advise here is if you want to donate, consider Autism West Midlands, Autistica, Resources For Autism just to name a few. They all take phone calls and are ready to provide support and assistance there and then. Much better than this so called "charity" now! (If I could really call them a proper charity)

I have an Autistic nephew and wanted to raise money to help raise awareness of Autism for the charity and his special needs school. I advised them what I was doing and why 9 months in advance, what ever I raised was 50/50. To cut the long story short, they lost my application form and my materials request. Even though I asked for them over the phone after chasing to see where they are, still got the order wrong. They advertised my challenge once on social media 3 months before the challenge. Never got in touch to see how I'm progressing. After my challenge was finished, I got no well done or thank you. The only message I got was "I will no longer work for the charity in a few days, but if you need anything contact my colleague". For me raising money for them, they weren't prepared to help me and I had to do all the chasing. The special needs school did 10 times more. Such a shame I have to put a negative comment to a charity. If they see this then hopefully they'll book their ideas up to encourage more people like me to raise money for the family's that need help.

Over the last couple of years, I've urgently needed support relating to our high functioning son whomhas Asperger's.  An important turning point came when he grew so frustrated at having to live home, life became difficuklt as my husband has sight and memory problems, etc. my own health had a downturn then. I wrote and telephoned yourself, leaving messages and to a couple of your nationwide links. The last time early in 2022 a receptionist answered my call and I was told everyone was working from home.   There is no support at all for helping him find work, assisted living, etc.  He had saved up after working to stay in Florida for several weeks, incurring debts and now the round of frustrations has all started again.  BALANCE in Tolworth/Surbiton no longer exists. A worker at Kingston Carers was very helpful and suggested ideas some of which I'm on process of taking up.       A supervisor at my husband's memory clinic could see the difficulties we faced at home and suggested I contact yourselves.  She spoke very highly of how the Society could arrange good coinselling for our son, etc. etc.  What a hope!!

Most of the workers are incompetent and lazy. For example, my recent mentor that I had today at university was very unhelpful and did not know what she was doing. When I asked for help with my verbal communication she said that she could not help me, and that she did not know what to do. We spent only 5 minutes for my appointment which was meant to be an hour, and she made me sign her sheet to confirm that it had been an hour so that she could be paid for doing no work. She basically sat there and said nothing and listened to what I said I needed help with and then said, "I can't help you". This is a pattern that I have noticed with the National Autistic Society workers. For example, when I was 10 years old I had a lot of social problems, could not talk, and had terrible anxiety, and when my parents and I asked what we could do to improve my social skills, they said the same thing that they could not help me. So we had to spend £50 every month for a private therapist to help me.

Truly the British equivalent of Autism Speaks.

If you happen to be neurodivergent, please avoid this "charity" at all costs.
If you are a Neurotypical parent, please do not send your child to this organisation, they will come out worse than they came in.
My particular experiences of NAS are from the North East of England branches, but I believe this isn't only limited to that area.
I was offered "help" from NAS for my social anxiety and assigned a worker by the name of Sarah Wallace.
Sarah was extremely unhelpful, rude and treated me in an extremely ableist manner.
The aim of Sarah was to try and get me to a social group that will also train with skills and sat me down, asking me extremely personal questions within the first day of meeting and downplaying my depression as "having bad days" and the extreme abuse I've suffered as "arguments."
I have no idea who in their right mind considered employing two workers to sit and fire personal and intrusive questions to anyone, especially a Neurodivergent person, however sadly being extremely intrusive and dehumanising seems the way most organisations deal with autism.
Sarah many times insulted me, having autism does not equal having low intellect and pressurised me into joining a training program I was clearly not comfortable with doing.
She said that if I were not to join this training program I would be "sitting around watching Netflix all day" and went as far as to turn up at my house uninvited, despite me clearly saying NO to her training.
I am tired of autistic people being treated as having no autonomy, we have every right to say no and her assumptions about my personal life, using this comment as one example of many felt deeply insulting to me.
Her guidance was to force me into a situation I was uncomfortable with and to make snide and unhelpful comments at my refusal.
And it appears I am not the only person who has been treated very poorly by this organisation, they are known for their abuse in residential care facilities.
If you search their services directory they have countless ABA practitioners listed, ABA is an extremely detrimental "therapy" and uses the same tactics as gay conversion therapy.
It's very clear that this society is not an advocate for us, I personally cut off my communication with Sarah before it got worse and I fully believe it would have.
NAS needs to do better, and it should not be up to us to thoroughly research every society before getting involved with it.
As long as you are employing people who believe it's okay to manipulate and bully and guilt trip their clients as well as the society being complicent with abuse, you will never be an advocate for neurodiversity.

My experience with Resources for Autism has unfortunately been extremely disappointing and frustrating. From the outset, the service has felt chaotic and poorly managed.

Firstly, the communication system is unnecessarily confusing. Having two separate phone numbers for London and Birmingham makes little sense. A single phone line with clear menu options would be far more effective. When I called, the staff member I spoke to seemed uninterested, unwilling to answer questions, and simply tried to pass me on. Staff should be trained and equipped with knowledge about both branches so that they can provide consistent, accurate information. Instead, I was left feeling dismissed and unsupported.

When I raised my concerns, I was told to email my details so someone could call me back. I waited over a month with no response. Only after I chased it up did anyone acknowledge my email. Even then, I was told that I shouldn’t have been promised a call in the first place—something I found very unprofessional. If a service promises to follow up, it should follow through. Ignoring emails—especially when they outline personal struggles and support needs—is unacceptable. A simple acknowledgment message or short response would have been far better than silence.

The overall handling of my case has been poor:
•	Promises were made that were not kept.
•	My email was ignored until I chased it.
•	Staff appeared untrained, disinterested, and inconsistent in their information.
•	Communication across the organisation seemed disjointed, from reception to admin to management.

I had real hopes that Resources for Autism could provide meaningful support. Instead, I felt let down, fobbed off, and left questioning whether an organisation that cannot manage basic communication is truly autism-friendly.

What should have happened is simple: someone should have explained what services are available, clarified the referral process, and set realistic expectations. That would have gone a long way to building trust. Instead, the lack of professionalism and broken promises have completely undermined my confidence in the service.

I strongly urge Resources for Autism to reflect on:
•	Communication processes (including phone lines and email responses).
•	Staff training, ensuring all staff can provide clear and consistent information.
•	Transparency about services offered, without overpromising or backtracking.
•	Building an approach that is genuinely autism-friendly, which means clarity, consistency, and reliability.

At present, my experience has been so negative that I would not recommend Resources for Autism. Unless these serious issues are addressed, others will likely feel the same disappointment and frustration that I did.

I reached out in february, because I felt the signs of an approaching autistic burnout. I was hoping to learn any copying mechanisms, or at least receive some sort of support / someone to talk to without judgement, which is according to their website something they take pride in.

The information provided was unfortunately hardly of any use, and I don't think they put me on the waiting list at all. They told me they'd get back to me in October for therapy. It is December as I am writing this and I still haven't heard back from them, even after reaching out per email last month...

In the end, I did burn out, lost my job, and now struggle to find a new one, which is exactly what I wanted to avoid by reaching out, so thanks for nothing!

reviews.text: I went with ADHD due to the good reviews, there are a lot of negative reviews but they all generally looked from a year ago and more. The more recent reviews seem positive so I went for it. Compared to other places which definitely were ‘dodgy’ I plumbed for the ADHD centre. The first and initial assessment was booked quickly and within weeks. I was diagnosed with ‘Inattentive ADHD’ and went down the medication route, at 56 I didn’t want to waste time. It’s not cheap, but getting my ADHD attended to was more important than money. I’m in the titration process and so far so good and I’ve had no issues with psychiatrist or the office staff. I see so many bad reviews that ADHD centre never got back to them or emailed back, why don’t these people just not pick up the phone. If you’re not happy with the psychiatrist they gave you, ask for another it’s not difficult… anyway, ADHD sucks!

Edit: having published this review I have had contact from the clinic who have to be fair been very apologetic and on request have refunded my money. I feel like my complaint was taken seriously and hope future assessments by the doctor I saw are much improved.

I have been so distressed by my ADHD assessment that I don’t know what to do. The Dr was rude and dismissive and as others have said, just racing through a tick box exercise impatiently, snapping at me “is it a yes or a no?”. The whole process was traumatic and I feel worse than ever. I’m not even willing to finish the process with them now, I feel completely helpless and like they just took my money and left me hanging in a terrible state.

I’ve had a truly awful experience dealing with this company. My “doctor” was late for every appointment, sometimes I was waiting on zoom for 20 minutes staring at a blank screen. Once the doctor arrived and was in the process of giving me life changing information, he appeared to be solely interested in box ticking without expanding on the clearly scripted questions or showing any concern for his patient in need. Consultations were over in 10 minutes (after having waited 20 minutes for the doctor) at a cost to me of about £20/minute. Sadly, this was just beginning.

I was started on the lowest possible doses of two medications, not the recommended doses. At first this seems like a responsible thing to do. However, each consultation is close to £200 plus the prescription from their private pharmacy was well over £100, totalling hundreds of pounds per consultation. The increments that they decided to increase my medication with each consultation were laughably small leading to many consultations. In hindsight, I have come to realise that at this point they were milking me for all the money they could get.

By the time I noticed the medication working (possibly placebo). I’d spent thousands, this left me with the decision to move forward with the treatment or have huge sunk costs. As a man desperately trying to improve his life, I decided to move forward only to find more costs and more pain.

Throughout the treatment process and on their website they speak of a “shared care agreement” between them and the GP which means no more consultations and 1/10th the cost of the prescribed medication via the NHS. On their site they ask you to discuss this agreement with your GP before embarking on the process, which I did. However, I could not be specific because I did not know the exact protocol which was to be recommended. I tried to get this sorted as soon as possible. After weeks of waiting for documents along with paying hundreds for the medication through the ADHD centre’s private pharmacy (another money spinner). I came to find that my GP does not in fact support this type of agreement at all, rarely do any doctors according to my GP. In my opinion, doctors do not do this type of thing as it increases their liabilities and they want to shield themselves from third party intervention as much as possible.

As one of the prescriptions is a medicine used regularly by the NHS, my GP could provide that one alone. Desperate, worn down from decades of pain for as long as I can remember and thousands of pounds down. I tried it the single medication. It was awful. I had constant sleepless nights, I do not wish to go in to further detail on a public page but just know that it was an extremely difficult time. When they contacted me guess what ? They wanted me to pay hundreds more for another consultation because I’d “stopped taking one of the medications”. I have spent thousands with this firm and I’m left with nothing. They prey on the mental weaknesses of the general public in order to generate profit. In my opinion, the dregs of society. I wish I could leave a 0 star review.

Dr. Rostamipour has gone above and beyond in caring for me. He truly listened to my concerns and approached my situation with a thoughtful, holistic perspective. His expertise and deep understanding have made an incredible difference—I feel better than I ever have. He has truly changed my life, and I couldn't recommend him more highly.

Dr Zadeh was lovely and listened to my answers and allowed me to elaborate without interruption. I am yet to start medication so cannot comment on the efficiency going forward. Overall, so far so good.

I am writing to express my deep disappointment following a recent experience with your organisation. My outreach was not for myself, but on behalf of a neurodiverse family member who is currently seeking employment and in need of support. I sought out a company like yours specifically because of your stated commitment to inclusion and support, but the experience we had was anything but supportive.

After uploading her CV to your website, we received no confirmation — not even an automated email. Concerned, we attempted to follow up by phone, only to be told via message that, due to high call volumes, you are unable to respond to all calls. While this was understandable, we were then advised to email instead, with the assurance that a team member would get back to us.

However, after sending the email, we received a reply stating that the company does not respond to emails either. At that point, it became clear that there was no viable way to communicate with your team at all. This complete lack of accessibility — being told not to call and then told you won’t respond to emails — left us both confused and frustrated.

Given the overwhelmingly positive reviews we had seen, our experience was shockingly inconsistent and left us feeling misled. Both my relative and I feel thoroughly let down. As such, we request that all of our personal data be removed from your website immediately.

This has been a total waste of time and a deeply disappointing experience, especially considering the vulnerability of those you claim to support. I sincerely hope your internal processes are reviewed to prevent others from going through the same.

One of the most commendable aspects of TfL is its extensive coverage. The network spans across the entire Greater London area, providing comprehensive connectivity through its buses, Underground (Tube), Overground, DLR (Docklands Light Railway), Trams, and River services. No matter where you need to go within the city, TfL has you covered, ensuring that you can reach your destination conveniently and reliably.

TfL's commitment to customer satisfaction is evident in the quality and frequency of its services. The Underground, in particular, operates with remarkable efficiency, with trains arriving at regular intervals, even during peak hours. The buses are a reliable mode of transportation, with extensive routes and accessibility features, making them suitable for people of all abilities. The Overground, DLR, Trams, and River services seamlessly integrate with other modes of transport, offering alternative and scenic travel options.

TfL's dedication to passenger comfort is noteworthy. Stations and vehicles are well-maintained and clean, ensuring a pleasant travel experience. The accessibility features, including step-free access, priority seating, and assistance for passengers with disabilities, demonstrate TfL's commitment to inclusivity and ensuring that everyone can travel with ease.

The Oyster card and contactless payment system introduced by TfL have revolutionized ticketing and made travel more convenient. The pay-as-you-go system, along with the daily and weekly fare caps, ensures that passengers are charged fairly, with no need to worry about purchasing individual tickets for each journey. Lastly, the customer service provided by TfL staff is exceptional. The employees are knowledgeable, helpful, and approachable, readily assisting passengers with inquiries, directions, and ensuring a safe and comfortable travel experience.

In summary, Transport for London (TfL) is a world-class public transportation network that plays a crucial role in keeping London moving. With its extensive coverage, efficient services, commitment to customer satisfaction, accessibility features, convenient ticketing options, sustainability initiatives, and outstanding customer service, TfL has truly set the benchmark for public transportation systems. reviews.text:
I started going to ENAS groups after coming to terms with being autistic later in life, although I really didn’t have a good time here and ended up leaving in the end. The whole thing just felt to clinical and patronising to me and I found myself feeling judged and disrespected for being autistic anyway which made me uncomfortable.

I also didn’t seem to get on with the woman who runs these groups either even though she apparently has a child with autism, which I felt may have been a big part of her motivation for being involved with NAS in the first place. In terms of trying to understand her own child and work out how high functioning they were in comparison to other autistic people, or even to try and fix autistic people in some sense and make them more ‘normal’ in quite an ambitious and egotistical way. Which is completely the wrong attitude to have about autism anyway as far as I am concerned, since you can’t be something that you are not or pretend to be a horse when you are really a zebra.

I don’t know if this is reflective of NAS in general or if it is just a problem with the Enfield branch, but I could tell that many of the ideas and approaches that they had to autism here were not really accurate at all or even verging on delusional. So if this is the general outlook that NAS has about autism, then I just find it amazing that they have absolutely no understanding or insight into this sort of thing and are this ignorant. As I found it to be undermining and insulting rather than helpful, even after I tried to bring up these issues and improve communication.

To make matters even worse though was the fact that one of the other people who was working for ENAS and seemed to be very much involved with it was someone who used to actually make fun of me for being autistic or projected his own issues about it onto me and was very nice at all, and also doesn’t seem to have changed that much during this time. But apparently ENAS doesn’t seem to notice these things and be aware of such attitudes, and so could even be potentially enabling abusive situations to happen. Since I even ended up feeling worse in some ways through having joined when I was really hoping for something that would be more helpful.

Never again will I turn to this so called centre of help and I would advise anyone doing so to have 0 expectations to avoid disappointment and upset.

I absolutely love the Neurodiversity Family Hub! Every week, my son and I take part in "My Junior Tribe".

I also volunteer as a support worker with the Tiny Tribe. The experience has been amazing. Working with preschoolers in Tiny Tribe is such a joy! They are incredibly smart, creative, and full of surprises. Just the other day they turned the water play tray into a water slide, which was so fun to watch!

What I really value is the chance to also connect with parents, especially those raising neurodiverse kids. Guiding and supporting them while learning from their experiences has been very rewarding. Every session teaches me something new, and I always leave feeling inspired and grateful to be part of such a nurturing, inclusive, and creative community.

Highly recommend the Hub to any family looking for support and connection!

Me and my son attend the tiny tribe playgroup every Wednesday morning and it’s absolutely brilliant. My son always has the best time and we really do recommend it 🥰 The workers are lovely and always make you feel welcome.

The ND Hub is an invaluable service for our ASD child, and welcomes siblings too. They have made so many friends and had fantastic experiences with the kind, experienced and brilliant team at the Hub. Spread the word!
The NFH is fantastic. They have supported me a lot. I value their advice and the service they providing for the community. The staff are very friendly and polite.

The Neurodiversity Family Hub is a beacon of hope for anyone with an interest in creating a more caring and inclusive society. Wherever you are on your journey of understanding neurodivergence, and all the challenges and opportunities it presents, the Neurodiversity Family Hub is there to help you. With their assistance our family has navigated huge obstacles that otherwise would have been insurmountable. The support we have received has been superb in every way. Hopefully at some point in the future, every community will have its own hub and benefit from the same flow of positivity and partnership.

reviews.text:
I have used the Asian Disabled Persons Association (APDA) care services for some time and am currently still under contract with them. I want to acknowledge that the standard of personal care I’ve received has generally been good — that’s not where the issue lies.

However, there are several recurring concerns around management, complaints handling, communication, and flexibility, particularly for service users on Direct Payments.

1. Lack of Management Accessibility
When there is a problem or complaint, it’s virtually impossible to get past the single point of contact assigned to you. Managers do not return calls, do not engage directly, and do not provide independent review or oversight. Everything is filtered through one person, which creates a closed system with no accountability or escalation route.

2. Misunderstanding of Direct Payment Arrangements
APDA often behaves as if the contract is still between them and social services, rather than between them and me as the Direct Payment holder. This causes confusion and breaches privacy boundaries, as they act as if they are accountable to social services when, in fact, my contract is directly with them.

3. Lack of Flexibility and Backup Care
There’s no operational flexibility when I need to adjust hours or arrange occasional extra support. They have limited or no backup care staff available, which leaves me without care and support when something unexpected happens.

This raises safeguarding concerns, as I have been left without care or support despite my needs being known and assessed. There’s no visible awareness of the risks this creates for a disabled client.

4. Profit Over People Mindset
Despite being described as a non-profit organisation, their behaviour often reflects a profit-driven mindset — focusing on payments and financial control rather than care continuity or client wellbeing. It makes me question whether the organisation’s stated values align with their actual practice.

In summary, while APDA can provide good care day-to-day, the organisation struggles when there’s a challenge, complaint, or need for flexibility. A good provider should be able to handle issues constructively, but in my experience, APDA resists change, transparency, and open dialogue.

result.name: Barbican Centre

reviews.text:
In all my years going to London, NEVER entertained The Barbican Centre....silly me!
Absolutely amazed at this great space, building, history, eateries, events & activities & landscape where concrete, water & greenery create surprising pleasure to the eye.

Great cosmopolitan chilled out vibes.
Watching your money, take a picnic! Free to enter The Barbican itself to have a mooch around 😍

Very big area and interesting experiment. It’s nice for the residents here to have a quiet zone in the center of a big city. But honestly the architecture doesn’t feel welcoming and walking down those big long corridors is a bit scary because there is not a single soul around as the shops area and the residence area are strictly separated (resembles many places in the US). On the other hand, the shopping area is nice. They have galleries, theaters, gift store with many unique products and a cafe (food is ok but the portion is abundant).

I recently visited for a work conference and completely forgot how special of a space the centre is, particularly in the city of London where it sticks out like a sore thumb.

The main event hall for one is spectacular with great views and acoustics, not to mention comfy seats (for the first hour).

The staff are very friendly if not high brow.

I was also surprisingly impressed by their toilets, but the best part is undoubtedly the outdoor space of the garden and pond area, which is open to the public (not the garden).

Highly recommend for a city lunch/chat if the weather is nice.

We recently made the trip down from the Midlands for a performance of 'Good Night, Oscar', which was superb. The theatre was a really great space with clean and comfortable seats and we had a nice view of the stage from the stalls. The acoustics were great, and we could hear every word (and note) without the actors having to shout. The way the set changes were managed was genius, with components sliding off the stage as new ones entered.

The wider centre was clean and tidy, and it was fairly easy to get around. The gift shop was well laid out and had a good variety of items for purchase. There was ample parking and it was reasonably priced for London (still expensive though). If you're driving, keep in mind the Barbican is in the congestion charging zone, which is currently at £17.50 per day.

We thoroughly enjoyed our visit, though next time we'll likely take the train to save a bit of money!

Don't miss this hidden green oasis with over 1,500 plant species—perfect for a moment of peace amidst greenery and water. Here, you'll find cafes, restaurants, and exhibition spaces, making it a place both vibrant and reflective.

The Barbican is a true treat for fans of high-end culture!

You invited Emma to promote her organisation Autistic Inclusive Meets Community Group Aim. Subject: Serious Concerns About Carers from Disability on Action – Please Read

I want to raise a serious complaint and make others aware of my recent experience with carers from Disability on Action, specifically a woman named Dee Dee.

When she first started, she came across as genuine and kind. But shortly after, her whole energy shifted. She became rude—especially toward me—stopped greeting me altogether, and often looked at me with a cold, unfriendly expression. Her behavior made me incredibly uncomfortable in my own home, which is unacceptable from someone in a caregiving role.

What’s even more concerning is that she brought along another woman named Tessie, who wasn’t even from a legitimate care agency. From what I was told, it was Dee Dee who got her involved through personal connections. That’s completely unprofessional and, frankly, dangerous when it comes to vulnerable people needing proper care.

Eventually, they both decided to leave, and honestly—it was for the best. I was holding back from saying something directly, but I feel it’s my duty now to speak up and warn others.

Dee Dee might appear like she cares, but actions speak louder than words. Bringing unqualified friends into care roles, and treating family members with disregard and disrespect, is not only wrong—it’s harmful.

To anyone looking for carers: please be cautious. Bad energy and fake people can slip into these roles, and if you’re not paying attention, they’ll drain your peace of mind and affect your home.

Name them and shame them? Yes—because people like this should not be trusted around vulnerable individuals. Don’t be fooled by fake smiles.

reviews.text: ADD-Vance has been a lifeline for my family. At a time when doors were closed to us, they listened, validated my concerns, and gave the best advice. The knowledge and support I gained from their team and courses have not only helped me cope and fight for my child but also support others along the way. Their QB Test gave us vital evidence that helped secure an EHCP, and my child is now thriving because of it. It has also helped us be taken seriously to be considered for diagnosis which was being constantly dismissed by professionals despite the severity of my child’s struggles to access their education. I cannot thank Georgia, Lisa, Amanda, Sophie, and the whole team enough — you’ve carried us through some of our darkest moments and celebrated the brighter ones with us. Feels nice to be out the other side of the storm thanks to ADD-Vance. There will always be something to fight for but we are so blessed to have this service I owe them my sanity and can’t thank them enough. ADD-Vance truly is vital for SEN parents, and services like this are essential to ensure families are heard, supported, and able to help their children flourish.

Normally I call and leave a message as i can't access e mail or see small screens. My hands also don't navigate online. I've spent weeks and months explaining myself over and over. I called another organisation - in 5 mins they offered me Telephone form filling with a scribe, no more than 1 question at a time, meetings face to face with a list for ND people - voice memos - with the same info in writing - questions in 1 liner 3's in bullet points or alpha or numerical order. The point is not only does it enable a range of disabled or comms needs before they escalate but it saves so much time in the long run. No need for repeating needs each time.

Then carried on a conversation when he should know working in disability when a person is upset and has cognitive stress as part of a cognitive condition. He didn't.  That is why "i find it difficult on the phone" as was remarked lime it is my probelm not the communicator  - it is Not due to my communication not being nuero typical or disability - it is because the phone communications are not nuero divergent accessible due to the reception being divisive - anti autism and not aware of invisible disabilites  - this fits in cognitive disabled friendly or accessibility at RUILS. Life is hard enough as it is without more of the same nuero typical ways of working. We accidentally stumbled across The Arts House in the Summer of 2024 when Joe and the team were on Sutton High Street offering free trial sessions when the school was in its infancy.  My daughter is obsessed with performing and having had not so great experiences at other schools (due to a lack of understanding of my daughters needs at the time) I was wary of taking up the trial session. Nevertheless we took the offer and I am so glad we did.  My little lady has excelled in her technique in all areas (Dance and Drama being her strong suits) and her confidence in herself and her abilities has exploded!! I’ve even had comments from her teachers at school say they have seen a change in her personality (for the good)

To Joe, Olivia, Phoebe, Rachel and the rest of the team.  The Arts House isn’t a business, it’s a safe space for the students to be themselves, to express and explore their love of performing among other like minded children who can do exactly the same. They make it feel like a family.  My daughter loves going to her classes every week and it’s so obvious from how happy the children are on arrival and collection that everyone is having a great time.

This evening was the end of year performance and it was so obvious the amount of hard work that had gone into it. Not by just the children but the adults to. It ran like a well oiled machine and I can’t wait to see what this next year will bring us!

So congratulations to all involved in making The Arts House the phenomenal success that it is fast becoming! You should all be very proud!!

We couldn’t be happier with our experience at the Arts House. From the very beginning, it was clear that this is more than just a place for drama, singing, and dancing lessons—it’s a true community. The team’s dedication, passion, and support have had such a positive impact on our daughter. She’s grown in confidence, developed her talents, and most importantly, found a place where she truly belongs.

The environment feels like a close-knit family. Every child is seen, encouraged, and celebrated, and that care shines through in everything they do. We’re so grateful to be part of this incredible group and can’t wait to see what the future holds. Thank you for inspiring and nurturing not just performers, but happy, confident individuals.

My children (5 and 8) have been going to the Arts House sessions for nearly a year now and we all love them. The kids have so much fun and are growing in confidence whilst we as parents trust the staff completely and find Joe the owner very accommodating, welcoming and caring. I really feel that we are part of a loving community and that the team genuinely care for the children.
My daughter struggles sometimes with going into clubs but the team are so fantastic with her and she always comes out feeling extra special on the hard days.
They recently put on the Summer production which was written by the team and it was brilliant - I found myself moved but the story and the team and  children worked so hard to put on a great show. Highly recommend to anyone looking for a performing arts class or just looking to find something to build their child's confidence!

The Arts House is a wonderful performing arts school. Our daughter has absolutely thrived here. The teachers are so dedicated and the communication is second to none.
She does 3 hours every Friday evening and is always excited to go even after a full week of school. She loves the opportunities she is given to perform. Highly recommend - Joe and team are absolute superstars and genuinely care and bring out the best in all of the students.

My daughter started around February time and she absolutely loves going every week. Seven months ago, I wouldn't have thought she would perform on stage as part of a big production, but thanks to Joe and his amazing team, she excelled, and her confidence has grown!! reviews.text:
I cannot recommend SEN talk highly enough. It really has been a lifeline since being introduced to the service a year ago. Annaliese, the director and founder is always there to listen and offers helpful, informative and supportive advice. She truly understands the challenges faced by families with children with additional needs and is always ready to help in any way she can.

The Lego therapy sessions my younger son attends has really helped improve his social communication skills and the support and help annaliese has given my older son whilst he has had difficulties at school has been invaluable.

This review really doesn't do SEN talk justice and if I could give 10 stars I would!! Amazing organisation!

When my son was diagnosed with ADHD and ASD last year I was completely overwhelmed and quickly found that there was not much support out there for my son, especially as he was high functioning. There was very little in my area that offered advice or services. After being told about everything Annaliese had created at Sen Talk I was instantly reassured and at ease after our first conversation. It is absolutely amazing what she has accomplished and provides for children and families that have children with SEN needs. I was fortunate to complete a parent course to help understand Sensory Issues and this has helped me immensely with helping my son on a day to day basis and understanding how his environment affects him and ways to reduce this. He also attends the Lego Club and really enjoys this and I can already see it has helped with his socialising skills. He is excited to turn 7 and join the communicate youth group head on a Friday and to go on his first trip with Sen Talk to godstone farm.

They also have mont coffee mornings and evening sessions where they have speakers for all difference specialist areas like  EHCPs, school exclusions, occupational therapist and more.

Sen Talk has been a lifeline for me and I know it is to so many children and families and I would highly recommend the services to everyone. It has been great to meet other parents that are having the same experiences as me and understand what you’re going through.

Thank you Sen Talk. Keep up the amazing work!!!

I have watched Sen Talk CIC grow into a fantastic resource for parents, carers and even Grandparents of children that are Autistic.
Annaliese will go above and beyond to make sure that all her families get exactly what they need to help them on their fabulous journey, I say fabulous because it is a very special journey and with the right tools to meet emotional and physical need it becomes a little easier. I am Noah's Grandmother and had no idea how to deal with what I thought behaviour problems. I am cringing  writing this :-( I have learnt such a lot been on many courses and seen amazing changes in the children and parents that have attended group sessions, training and especially Lego based therapy... Amazing charity, keep up the good work !

Brilliant service for children and their families with SEND.
If you have a child with ADHD or autism definitely worth going too.

reviews.text: This is a lovely looking pub. I was pleasantly surprised that it had table service and the waitress was very nice and friendly.  We got our drinks and placed our order fine. The vegetables and Yorkshire pudding was fine but the meat was awful. It was fatty and the little meat i could eat was like leather. My sons fish and chips looked lovely and he said it was nice. As someone working in the industry, I found the quality far below expectations: The lamb shank was dry and unpleasant in texture, the burger was burnt, the Sunday roast sirloin, which should have been served pink, arrived well-done and overly dry, the Yorkshire puddings were dense and super dry, lacking the lightness they should have.

Overall, it was a very poor dining experience for my family and me. With better attention to service and food standards, this place could improve significantly, but as it stands, I would not recommend it.

Seems to be a lack of staff these days.
A real shame as it’s walking distance or really handy if coming back on the tube.

reviews.text: The outdoor pool at David Lloyd Bushy is very clean and well maintained, which makes swimming really enjoyable. The changing rooms are also clean and tidy, which is great. The only small downside is that not all of the stands have hair straighteners, but overall the facilities are excellent.

I usually don’t leave reviews, but I felt compelled to share a very disappointing experience I had as a guest at David Lloyd Bushey.

I arrived at the club on a valid guest pass, invited by my brother, a member who was running a few minutes late. Despite explaining the situation, I was spoken to by the front desk staff in a rude and patronising manner. They refused to let me inside and insisted I wait awkwardly at the entrance after I had gone in through the barrier already using my guess pass , even though my sister-in-law—also a member—was already inside the club. Shockingly, they insisted that she physically come out to collect me, as if I were a child or security risk.

I completely understand that clubs have rules, but what was missing here was simple human decency, flexibility, and any semblance of customer service. I was left standing there while members walked by, feeling embarrassed and publicly singled out for no valid reason. All it would have taken was a little empathy or discretion—perhaps allowing me to wait in the lobby for a few minutes until my brother arrived.

This experience made me feel not only unwelcome but also judged and belittled. The rigid and dismissive attitude of the staff is unacceptable, especially in a place that markets itself as a premium health and leisure club.

I urge David Lloyd to review how their staff are trained to deal with guest scenarios and consider the importance of discretion and dignity in customer interactions. Not every situation needs to be met with rigid enforcement of rules—sometimes, kindness and basic courtesy go a lot further in creating a positive experience.

Unfortunately, this left a very bad impression, and I would seriously think twice before recommending the club to friends or family

I absolutely love David Lloyd Bushey! The facilities are top-notch, and the atmosphere is always welcoming. The outdoor jacuzzi is a real highlight—perfect for relaxing after a workout. The sauna is spacious and well-maintained, offering the ideal way to unwind. The swimming pool, both indoors and outdoors, is fantastic, always clean and at a great temperature.

The staff are friendly, professional, and always happy to help. The club is well-kept, and the variety of fitness classes keeps things exciting. Whether you’re looking to exercise, relax, or socialize, this place has it all.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for a premium health club experience!

Staff ignoring service users, staff talking in their own languages, staff leaving service users unattended for long periods of time when they are supposed to be on constant 1:1, shift leaders giving themselves easier duties, not enough drivers on shift, Rotas being changed at the last minute, day staff taking on night work due to lack of staff, sub-par cleaning of the home , staff cliques, seniors and management being part of the cliques, cliques making life difficult for professional carers, vehicles dirty inside and out, staff not being fully trained, staff being employed who cannot speak or write English and lack of food for service users.

I would stay clear of this organisation as a whole. Staff are overworked and chronically underpaid. They are understaffed and patients are abandoned. Stay clear and look elsewhere.

Since moving into Edwina Place in April 2022 there has been nothing but persistent negligence. Members of staff using their power to pray on the vulnerable. Sexual remarks and gestures were made. Physical unwanted touch. Brainwashed to think that it’s ok to meet staff outside of the home. Watched and laughed at while actively suicidal. Uncalled  for comments on appearance and self harm scars. Medication overdoses. Forgetting to give medication. Given the wrong medication. Not having required medication. Money has been stollen. Verbal abuse and intimidation. The list goes on. Unless you want to add to your trauma do not move here. I’ve been forced to leave the home in no fault of my own, but I cannot guarantee my safety there. reviews.text: This place was hired by one of the Bollywood dancing institutes and we visited to watch their performance.  Place has good facilities and cafes on each floor. Comfortable seats. Their theatre appeared to be newly renovated. We enjoyed our visit.

Brilliant and modern place to host various events / theatre and disable friendly. It has cafe also. Great for events with service lift / bar area and kitchen for catering .

Staffs are friendly , u can take drinks inside with lid on.

The artsdepot in Finchley is a must-visit for its varied shows suitable for all, playing a central role in the community and offering chances for artistic development. It's a place where culture thrives, supporting the arts means maintaining a vibrant creative scene. The venue boasts up-to-date amenities and is fully accessible, positioned in a well-connected area of North London. Supporting it bolsters the local economy. Plus, live performances here promise singularly thrilling experiences, enriching both the cultural fabric and personal enjoyment.

Was looking forward to seeing a play at the arts depot on Friday 25th of April, Just between ourselves by Alan Ayckebourn. However, our enjoyment was marred by feeling cold all evening and I noticed on leaving that the lady at the back who shows you the seats had a little radiator next to her to keep her warm. We got the impression that they are severely cutting back on costs as the bar for the theatre is never opened when I have visited,  one has to go downstairs to the café to get a drink in the interval, the escalator has been turned off to save costs which is probably a good idea as there are lifts and stairs. Also, the soap dispensers in the ladies were all empty apart from one and the hand dryers barely worked in that one of them came on and then turned off almost immediately. I couldn’t get the other one to turn on. It seems an awful shame that a theatre which showed so much promise appears to be so disappointingly hard up!

Worst Princess was good, great sound and singers. Kids liked it, especially he dragon at the end.

I know it's probably looked down upon to say but it was let down by a couple who brought their baby even though the play was 3+ and he cried most of the way through, particularly when there was singing as I think it was too loud for him. They never took them out to calm him down so was very distracting for surrounding families.

editorial_summary.overview: Modern museum with a re-created Victorian Jewish Quarter, historical artefacts & Holocaust tales.

result.formatted_address: First Floor Office, Residential Tower, 353-359 Finchley Rd, London NW3 6ET, UK
result.name: Jewish Museum London

reviews.text:
The Jewish museum is a hidden gem of a museum.
It is important to check the museum website for opening times and tickets etc.
As a non Jew I found the museum a treasure trove of Jewish life and history on this island.
Of interest is the exhibition of the lived experience of Judaism in the UK. And the important contribution of Jews to British life. An essential part of the solero of British life history.
The Holocaust is narrated through the eyes of a British Jew who found himself and his wife caught up in the madness of antisemitism. His testimony is moving as are the artifacts of life in these camps.
A visit is very recommended.

I really enjoyed my visit here and learnt alot about the history and culture of Jews in Britain from the first settlers who came over in 1066. The entry price is very fair, £8.50 Adult and £6.50 concession.
The museum itself has three floors each with a different aspect of Jewish culture. The top floor is currently dedicated to the artistic work of Charlotte Salomon describing her life through a chronological set of paintings.
The 2nd floor is devoted to the history and culture associated with Jewish settlement in England and is the core of this museum. It also houses a section on the holocaust.
On the first floor you have all the beautiful Jewish religious artifacts, many focused on the Torah, the holy book.

this museum is a nice place for people who wants to learn about the jews. as a jew,it was nice to see  the exhibition ,but the information wasn't much useful.
History of jews in Britain was nice,but the 3rd floor exhibition of pictures that was when i was there (this floor seems to change from time to time) was boring for me at least.
There is a class there,suitable for schools or universities that want to learn a bit about Judaism, but Judaism is much more than showed there...

Very well-organized. With detailed captions. You could learn a lot about the Jewish culture and traditions and it sort of demystifies them. (It is so informative that I could not finish all of them on one go!)

Small but well planned displays covering many aspects Jewish life from medieval times till the present.
Helpful staff,lift and toilets clearly marked plus a small cafe. Worth a visit.

editorial_summary.overview: Free-admission museum in a Victorian house & modern extension, dedicated to local history & culture.

result.formatted_address: Oaklands Park, Moulsham St, Chelmsford CM2 9AQ, UK
result.name: Museum of Chelmsford

reviews.text: It's a very good spot to visit with kids, especially if you want to learn about British history as well. There are sections of the natural museum, Marconi inventions, the Essex army regiment, and a drawing and history area of prehistoric, Anglo-Saxon, Roman, and modern sections. Half a day is enough. There is a park in front for a picnic and a play area at the back for children. There is a cafe on site.

Great place to visit. Super friendly staff. It is a tad small but it’s got lovely things to see. It was nice and quiet when we visited. Definitely would recommend getting there early to get a car spot in the car park. There is a toilet at the car park and in the museum

A delightful museum where the focus on the Roman presence in Chelmsford makes up quite an interesting part of the place. Chelmsford also being the birthplace of radio means there's a fascinating learning space to understand and digest said information and it's hugely informative. Other exhibits focus on the city's role during the war (the mannequins here are excellent) as well as educational films about how Chelmsford came to be - do look out for the room detailing the complete timeline as well as snippets of facts about this storied city as well as the notable characters that shaped it all. Plenty for the kids to get stuck into and all of it is free! Would definitely recommend.

A lovely, free to access museum situated within the beautiful grounds of Oaklands Park.
It's got a great selection of local history to see and interact with.
The kids especially like the live bees hive they have on the first floor that allows access through the exterior wall. (The bees have been here since I was a little girl too, yet the museum has come along way over the years).
They have a small museum shop at the entrance too, aswell as a donation box.
There's free parking on site, although beware on weekdays there's a limited parking time allowance of two hours.
With public toilets nearby and an excellent cafe with inside seating and outside tables to enjoy the sunshine, whilst overlooking the large parks situated at the back, you can easily enjoy a cuppa whilst keeping an eye on the children.
This all makes for a lovely, low cost afternoon out with the family on a sunny day.

Wow! What a wonderful place! We visited for the first time today, and to be truthful, I didn't know what to expect, but I have to say, I was very impressed, by everything! First, you get two free hours of on site parking, second the grounds of the Museum are lovely; grass, trees, picnic benches and tables, and great play areas for the kids. There is also a nice-looking cafe with both indoor and outdoor seating. The Museum building itself is also very attractive,  inside and out and the exhibits are wonderful! So much to see and many hands on, activities for both adults and children! This has got to be my Chemlsford 'happy place!' I can't wait to go back! Lovely staff too! 😉

We were invited to this place for a wedding and it was really cool. The building is a former church which was renovated and is now a mix between cafe/bar and private event location. On the ground floor, the space was open for public and there was a bar with drinks and some snacks. The wedding reception itself happened on the upper floor. We were around 100 people which was a perfect size for this place.
We can recommend this place for private events like weddings, birthdays etc.

I’d been past here so many times as an adult and always wanted to see something, so fortunately I was able to a few weeks ago. The staff were all friendly and Diverse, the vegan treats were tasty, the hot drinks fabulous and the show was one of the best I’ve seen. Highly rated place with great content, worth your time to come and see something here or even just get a tea and cake and relax.

Nice theatre ,very organised ,modern .the cafe bar is super efficient and with good prices .
Easy access from tube .
Wonderful renovated space in an old church - wheelchair (and pram) accessible with lots of great events and classes for children. There’s also a cafe inside which does good coffee.

Truly a wonderful place for children and adults. It offers a variety of creative workshops, engaging events, and friendly staff who always make you feel welcome. The atmosphere is warm and inspiring, and there is always something interesting happening for people of all ages. I highly recommend visiting this if you want to learn, have fun, and feel part of the community.

Lovely staff and volunteers, who look after the children and young people with great care. Produce fantastic productions.

reviews.text:
It was my first time at this museum and I really enjoyed my visit.
It is quite small but has a very good selection of historical artifacts. The world section was good. The music room was incredible. There were so many different instruments displayed. You don't have to pay to enter the museum but there sections you need a paid ticket to view like the aquarium and the butterfly garden or greenhouse. I only visited the aquarium on this visit. I bought a ticket from the reception, it was only £6 which was good. The aquarium was in the basement floor and was nice. They had a good selection of sea life, that were amazing to see. I think the last time for entry on both the butterfly house and the aquarium is 4 or 4:30 pm.
I didn't make it to the zoo and did not even realise they had it until later. Hopefully I'll see it next time.
I loved the gardens and I'm glad I came during the summer to experience it's beauty. Overall it was a great way to spend the afternoon. I would visit again.

This museum and garden in Forest Hill, South London, is free and family-friendly.

The garden features many benches and shaded areas, making it a great place to relax. There is also a beautiful sunken garden that invites exploration and leisurely strolls.

You can find exhibitions on musical instruments, natural history, and anthropology. Additionally, there is a butterfly house and a small aquarium that visitors can enjoy for a fee.

Highly recommend visiting here

What a great museum! Lots of interesting items from all over the world, good descriptions and explanations of everything too. We went in holiday time and there were a lot of kids running around but there's plenty of space inside and outside. The cafe is excellent too. We could have spent the entire day here, the museum, not just the cafe!

We visited the park and the free sections of the museum. The park, parts of which currently under renovation, is somewhat smaller than we thought but the view is nice. The museum is also compact but contains a very good and interesting collection of items about anthropology, natural history and musical instruments. You can easily spend a whole afternoon which the exhibition. In fact parts of the museum is under renovation too and it should be even more worth visiting afterwards. Overall it is a good place for family. Roadside car parking on nearby streets.

A fantastic space for a visit with children. The cafe was great. The aquarium was loved by the children. I wasn't bowled over by the butterfly room but it was an interesting experience. The Park surrounding it is also so lovely.
