reviews.text:
A lovely little theatre, my 5 year old really enjoyed The Paper Dolls.

Venue staff are very warm and welcoming, the puppeteers extremely talented and engaging. The show was clearly well rehearsed and very slick, considering the multiple themes throughout.

Will definitely be looking to see what is on in the future and come back.
We loved the bear hunt. It was spectacular. Our 2 year old was totally captivated and so were we.

Lovely experience. Went with a 4 and 6 year old to see The Everywhere Bear and they both loved the performance, it was entertaining and engaging. The theatre is small, with no allocated seating. We were the last ones to arrive and could still sit together, since it was not overcrowded. Would definitely go back!
Beautiful little theatre with cushioned pew seats with child seats in the middle. A lovely place to take the little ones.

Thoroughly enjoyed a performance of paper dolls here. My niece loved it and even stayed til the end to tell them all what a great job they did. A nice event of you're looking to fill your day for your little ones.

editorial_summary.overview: Large theatre with a remarkable musical and dramatic history, home to The Lion King since 1999.

result.formatted_address: 21 Wellington St, London WC2E 7RQ, UK
result.name: Lyceum Theatre

reviews.text: Absolutely incredible show! Highly recommend. We sat in the first balcony and it was excellent view! They hire out binoculars for a fee of £1 but didn't need it from our seats. The theatre decor is absolutely beautiful inside and out. The show is one of the best I have seen! My only issue would be they encourage everyone to turn up earlier to the show but don't open the doors for everyone to get their seats so everyone is crammed into the small bar area waiting to be let in rather than it be a staggered entrance and less crowding.

We went to see The Lion King musical, and it was my first time experiencing it. The show was incredibly impressive and beautiful – I even cried a lot! The touches of humor here and there were also really enjoyable.

It truly was a top-class musical, and I would recommend it to everyone.

Grand old theatre with gorgeous interiors. Big enough to have a nice capacity, intimate enough to feel close to the performers. Not so much for the theatre, but we saw the Lion King and it was spectacular, and went off without a hitch which I imagine was logistically complicated and a testament to the theatre’s staff in addition to the group company. I only took off a star after seeing multiple mice run through the aisles, which certainly caused a bit of a stir.

Beautiful theatre to watch Lion King! Loved the intricate details on the walls and ceiling it added to the event. I wished there was more light in the audience before the show so I could see the details a bit more clearly. My tickets were high up in the grand balcony and when I mean high it was high close to nose bleed. I don’t know if there were elevators - it wasn’t offered to me and I was dead climbing up the stairs so note to people with mobility issues it will be difficult to go to the upper level. I wasn’t sure if my seats were too high to enjoy and no it was still perfect. Very clear view and sound was amazing. Seats are not the most comfortable and everything is a bit squished. If people come late you are constantly getting up to let people by which was frustrating. You can rent binoculars to see stage better. It wasn’t needed but rented anyway for the experience which was fun. Theatre offers drinks and some snacks wish it was a better selection. Overall thoroughly enjoyed the experience!

Best show I’ve seen so far. A must do. Great performance and great actors. We were sat around the centre of grand circle and view was perfect. There is a small break half way through the show and binoculars are available on every seat for 1£ rental

editorial_summary.overview: World's leading museum of urban transport with galleries of vintage London trams, trains & buses.

result.formatted_address: London WC2E 7BB, UK
result.name: London Transport Museum

reviews.text: The London Transport Museum is an absolute delight for all ages! It beautifully showcases how London’s transport system evolved — from horse-drawn carriages to iconic red buses and the Underground. The exhibits are interactive, informative, and very well presented. The vintage vehicles and classic Tube designs bring back nostalgia, while the hands-on sections make it perfect for kids too. A must-visit for anyone curious about London’s past and how its world-famous transport network came to life!

History & revolution of London transport system. Kids friendly museum they will love this place. It has also the history of transport system how they developed year after year from horse riding car to automated car now. Kids have a opportunity to make fun & play. Restaurants, shopping market, street funshow available here. The nearest train station is Leister for piccadilly line next to china town.

Such an interesting museum. Includes all different transport methods and has been made for anyone who has an interest in transport. I went on my own as an adult and really enjoyed it.
Staff super friendly and helpful. Also £25 to access for a year is very reasonable.
Only bit of advice, don’t go in summer holidays, there were lots of children running around with parents that didn’t care which dampened my experience but I know that the museum can’t help this.

Nestled in Covent Garden, the London Transport Museum is a great place to visit if you dig London  transit. Inside are a bunch of nice exhibits and full sized vehicles. Some of which you can go into, some of which you can't. This isn't the largest museum, but the location can't be be beat. Kids will love this museum too as there is plenty for them to do, including a play area.

A Interesting museum with lots to see and learn. Different buses, information about the underground, story about the Windrush, old taxis, Exhibitions, information about climate change, different maps on the underground plus much more things to see. It has more stuff upstairs and there is 2 floors so it is a decent size. I enjoyed going there and it has become one of my favourite museum's.

result.formatted_address: Upper Ground, London SE1 9PX, UK
result.name: Lyttelton Theatre

reviews.text:
Part of The National Theatre complex. Large auditorium with raked floor and large stag
Staff. Helpful and friendly.
Show. Here We Are. An excellent musical play. Stand performance amongst an excellent cast for me is Tracie Bennett.

Saw Inter alia with Rosamund Pike etc al. An excellent play about a female judge who has to manage work and home and the parental relationship with son and spousal relationship where she is the more successful.
Rosamund Pike occupies the stage through and never falters.
From the pen of Suzie Miller, without giving the ending the plan is about moral truth and legal truth. Must see.

One of my fave places in one of my fave London areas. Admittedly the show itself wasn’t my favourite but the experience was brilliant. If you are coming to see something at this theatre, come early and spend the day! There is space to work with your laptop, plenty to eat, good toilet facilities, and beautiful views and lots to see outside. Staff are very friendly and helpful too. Accessibility aids are visible and easy to get hold of.

The shop is great too. They have some books that I haven’t seen elsewhere and I got some honey from their very own bees!
Saw Inter Alia, which I cannot recommend more. Absolutely fantastic. The Theatre was well organised, and had a good drinks and snacks selection at the Bar.

Great theatre, very comfortable seats, no bad views wherever you sit.

Great play and performance.  Would highly recommend a visit.
I went to see Here we Are Again. I have mixed feelings about the show. The seats are a bit cramped for my taste. Olivier Theatre is a lot more comfortable.

editorial_summary.overview: Artifacts & interactives chronicle London's turbulent history from pre-Roman to modern times.

result.formatted_address: 150 London Wall, Barbican, London EC2Y 5HN, UK
result.name: Museum of London

reviews.text: There is no clear flow to some parts of the museum & I think like it would be really easy to miss bits. The staff were friendly & they had some good pieces in there. They could do with making it a bit interactive for kids. Took a couple of hours to walk though it all.

It's free. So that's a bonus. You can make a donation. They ask for £5 and it's worth it.
It was great to learn more about the city that I've lived in for nearly my whole life. I've never been before. I should've gone before. It's not just for tourists.
I was enticed to come by the Harry Kane exhibit and I loved it. It was amazing to see all the other exhibits that they have.
Would highly recommend it.
The place has moody lighting. It's not a bright museum. Actually I would say it's dark inside.

London has some of the best museums in the world and so many of then are free to boot.
This museum is well set up to tell the story of of London from prehistoric times all the way into the modern Era. Each section highlights major events, technologies, and traditions to illustrate the corresponding time period. The medieval section and the women's suffrage exhibits particularly captured my attention.

Really interesting exhibition about the history of London. Lots of really interesting artefacts to see and a few videos to watch. This is not really suitable for young kids, but would be great for teenagers and adults. A really great video about world war 2, but it is extremely sad. Lovely cafe at the entrance too. Well worth a visit.

Museum has some good and some kinda boring exhibits. However this is personal choice. For me, not being a Londoner it wasn't all for me. However was very informative. I preferred the later part where there was more fun things there. I did feel the guy explaining they were a charity at the beginning a bit much. We and I'm sure most people understand that these places are relying on funding and donations. However we would prefer to donate in peace without feeling forced. After all the tickets were free, it's the least we can do is spare money for them. As I'm sure most will feel the same.

editorial_summary.overview: Privately owned Edwardian theatre, hosting Agatha Christie's The Mousetrap since 1974.

result.formatted_address: West St, London WC2H 9NZ, UK
result.name: The Mousetrap at St. Martin's Theatre

reviews.text: Amazing place. We watched Mousetrap here in mid Jun 2025 and it was really a lovely theater. Old world charm, very well kept and our seats in the last row of Dress circle had perfect view too. Audio was crystal clear.

This ironic gem of a theater is an amazing place to see the world famous play The Mousetrap. It’s a very intimate setting, easy to navigate, and is a pleasure to watch the play unfold. What an amazing night out.
Saw the iconic mouse trap. Longest running play (who done it ) . Amazing theatre. Very traditional. Love the feel of this theatre.

Watching The Mousetrap in London was an unforgettable experience! Hard to believe this play has been running in the West End since 1952 and just recently celebrated its 30,000th performance – no wonder it’s the world’s longest-running play. The atmosphere in the theatre is unique, the cast was fantastic, and the suspense kept me hooked right until the brilliant twist at the end. You really feel like you’re part of theatre history when you see it. A must-see in London if you love mystery and great storytelling!

I went to see Benjamin Button here with some friends and family and had the most amazing time. The show is highly, highly recommended—the actors did an incredible job bringing the story to life.

The theater itself is lovely—so clean and welcoming. The food was great too, with a nice selection of crisps and beer, which made the evening even more enjoyable. It was a new experience for me, and I’m already looking forward to coming back. Definitely recommend this place for a fantastic night out!

result.formatted_address: National Maritime Museum, London SE10 9NF, UK
result.name: Ahoy! Play Area

reviews.text:
It’s a free kids play space and we absolutely loved it. It’s so well done and the kids had so much fun exploring different areas of maritime history. Our favourite was the Ship, and going insider the cabins was great fun. I will happily be going back again. Highly recommend this space.
Tickets have to be booked in advance, but they are free during the week during term time.

Make sure you pre-book online! You will be dissappointed if you don't. The first time we came here my son was so upset to leave, 45 minutes was not long enough for him! So today I booked him in for 2 slots and that was more than enough- we actually left before our time was up. Lots to explore for various ages, even babies as there is a sensory area. Outside the Ahoy! Play area there is a child friendly gift shop which are somewhat reasonably priced. Toilets are nearby although they are pretty much always busy. If you happen to have a potty training toddler- have a portable wee bottle handy!
Amazing place, especially the free sessions. Lots for kids to do, well managed, and one entry/exit for peace of mind!
We loved every minute of it. All the employees and the actual space were great.

This place is amazing!  I see people have been complaining that the slots are only 45 min, however it's so cheap (free on weekdays or £6 for 1 adult and 1 child), so we tend to book more than one slot, and get a snack in between.  Highly recommend this place, as it's my daughters favourite soft play.

editorial_summary.overview: Palladian mansion hosting world-class art exhibitions and a legendary open-submission summer show.

result.formatted_address: Burlington House, Piccadilly, London W1J 0BD, UK
result.name: Royal Academy of Arts

reviews.text: I've been to RA several times. This time, I'd like to share some of my feelings about the new exhibition and my evaluation of this location. First of all, I want to praise the staff at the front desk. A lady greeted me with a very gentle and warm smile when I was buying a ticket, which made the entire experience start on a good note. Then we needed to walk through a long exhibition area to another building to see the exhibition. The content of the exhibition was actually not much, and from multiple perspectives, I think Van Gogh's works are far superior to the other ones. The store area after the exhibition was very pleasant to browse, and the design of the souvenirs was very interesting.

Visiting the Royal Academy of Arts in London was a deeply enriching experience, marked by standout exhibitions that left a lasting impression. The Kerry James Marshall retrospective was a profound journey through his dynamic exploration of Black identity and history, showcasing his powerful storytelling through vivid, captivating works. Equally compelling was the joint exhibition featuring Anselm Kiefer and Van Gogh, where Kiefer’s monumental, texture-rich paintings contrasted beautifully with Van Gogh’s emotive brushwork, creating a striking dialogue between the two masters across time. The visit was not only visually stunning but intellectually stimulating, offering a rare opportunity to witness the convergence of contemporary and classic artistic genius in one remarkable institution.

Great place to pop in and visit. They have areas free of charge as well as pay areas. The Royal Academy of Arts (RA) is an art institution based in Burlington House in Piccadilly London, England. Founded in 1768, it has a unique position as an independent, privately funded institution led by eminent artists and architects. Its purpose is to promote the creation, enjoyment and appreciation of the fine arts through exhibitions, education and debate.

A little disappointed with this visit. I was expecting to see a lot of pre-raphaelite works, like the Mermaid by Waterhouse, which is listed as part of Royal Academy of art collection, however the permanent collection on display had very few artworks and only occupied one room, plus some good sculptures downstairs. Temporary exhibition of Van Gogh/Kiefer was quite nice. On the left hand side of the main entrance, Society of Antiquaries had a really informative exhibition of Magna Carta, with a lot of portraits and documents on display (the last 5 photos of this review), make sure to visit if you are in the area.

Loved my first visit to The Royal Academy so went for my second.
There was a temporary summer exhibition on which was excellent. The art pieces were so varied im pretty sure there would be something for everyone.
Also visited the Children's free exhibition. The talent and variety of the exhibits were outstanding.
Also went to the cafe which was a welcome break after spending a good 2 hours there.
I will be back.
Unbelievably in all the times I have been to London i have never been to The Royal Academy of Arts.
I went with a friend who has membership and I thought it was going to be a bit stuffy.
I was wrong there are the usual traditional galleries but we also visited some modern temporary exhibits which were brilliant.  Well laid out, vibrant, interesting and thought provoking.
They have a lovely bright cafe and a great shop
well worth a look.

editorial_summary.overview: Home to prominent theatre company presenting new plays, classic drama and Shakespeare productions.

result.formatted_address: London SE1 9PX, UK
result.name: National Theatre

reviews.text: Very inspiring atmosphere, impressive connection speed, and plenty of seating. The entrance is free (bag search). Gets a bit busy about 30 min before the performance (currently Inter Alia with Rosamund Pike). The building is a notable example of post-WWII Brutality architecture. While its radical minimalism and anti-aesthetics is not for everyone, it was fitting well the post-WWII resources deprivation and priorities re-evaluation (i.e. the shift from pompous public projects to NHS and other projects that prioritize human lives). Creative night lighting, both inside and outside, adds an extra visual appeal while preserving the core concepts of the style.

An absolute masterpiece of brutalist architecture, with an incredible use of space, well worth a visit, even if you don’t see a play. Lots of wonderful places to eat, drink and sit. The bookstore is fabulous.  Pictures don’t really capture it.

Visiting the National Theatre in London was a truly enriching experience. From the moment I entered the building, I was struck by the architectural elegance and the welcoming, vibrant atmosphere. The space manages to feel both grand and intimate, with thoughtful design that invites you to slow down, observe, and soak in the cultural energy.

I attended a performance of [insert name of the play or production here], and it exceeded all my expectations. The direction was sharp, the pacing flawless, and the performances from the cast were deeply compelling. Every actor brought nuance and authenticity to their roles, and the emotional weight of the story was palpable throughout the auditorium.

What stood out most to me was the staging and set design—visually stunning, with clever transitions and lighting that enhanced the narrative without ever overshadowing it. The sound design and live music (if applicable) were also beautifully integrated, creating an immersive environment that kept the audience fully engaged.

The National Theatre staff were professional and courteous, helping to create a smooth and enjoyable experience from beginning to end. Even the intermission felt like part of the magic, with spaces to relax, grab a drink, and discuss what we’d seen so far.

In short, the National Theatre delivers not just a show, but an entire journey. It’s a place where powerful storytelling, artistic innovation, and human connection converge. I left the theatre inspired, moved, and already planning my next visit.
This national institution is the best theatre in London. I enjoy the awesome architecture everytime I visit the National Theatre. The sound quality in the auditorium is spectacular.

Great coffee, super location right beside the Thames, cheap underground car parking, lots of spaces with easy road access by Westminster Bridge, used just park app entry/exit via number plate recognition a very easy process, pastries were nice and fresh, good location to work from, lots of tables and chairs too, good security with a bag search on the way in and very helpful polite staff.. great ambience..

editorial_summary.overview: Family-friendly exhibits with a variety of sea creatures (most offer play areas & group packages).

result.formatted_address: Riverside Building, County Hall, Westminster Bridge Rd, London SE1 7PB, UK
result.name: SEA LIFE London Aquarium

reviews.text:
I recently visited the SEA LIFE Aquarium in London and had a wonderful experience. The exhibits are well-designed, with a wide variety of marine life from sharks and rays to colorful tropical fish. The layout makes it easy to explore, and I especially enjoyed the underwater tunnel—it really felt like walking through the ocean!

The staff were friendly and knowledgeable, always ready to answer questions and share interesting facts. Everything was clean, well-organized, and family-friendly. It’s a perfect spot for both kids and adults to enjoy and learn about marine creatures.

I definitely recommend a visit if you’re in London and looking for a fun and educational experience.

Surprisingly magical — penguins, jellyfish, and sharks all in one place

I wasn’t sure what to expect, but SEA LIFE London Aquarium really impressed me. The layout flows nicely, and each section feels like stepping into a different world. The penguins were a highlight — playful and oddly calming to watch. The jellyfish room was stunning, like floating through a neon dream. And the shark tunnel? Genuinely thrilling. Seeing them glide overhead was surreal.

It’s not massive, but it’s packed with variety and atmosphere. Great for escaping the noise of the city for a couple of hours. Definitely worth a visit if you’re into marine life or just want something a bit different.

A great experience with amazing sea life, from sharks to penguins. The displays are beautiful and staff are friendly and knowledgeable. It’s fun and educational for all ages, but the ticket prices are quite high for the time spent inside. Still worth visiting at least once! 🐠🐧🌊

The London Sea Life Aquarium is a fantastic spot for families, couples, and anyone curious about marine life. The exhibits are well laid out, with everything from colorful tropical fish and jellyfish to sharks and turtles. Walking through the glass tunnel surrounded by rays and sharks is definitely a highlight. It’s educational as well as entertaining, with plenty of information about conservation and protecting our oceans. it’s a great experience overall and well worth a visit.

We visited the London Sea Life Aquarium with two six-year-olds. We arrived around 10 a.m. and spent nearly four hours there, walking through at a relaxed pace with the kids. Overall, it was an enjoyable outing — the kids were especially fascinated by the turtle shell presentation and loved the chance to touch it. The ray tank was another highlight, and the large aquarium with sharks and sea turtles was truly mesmerizing — both for the children and adults.

That said, there were a few drawbacks. The ocean tunnel is very short, and the penguin nursery was partly closed. We had to lift the kids up so they could see the penguins, which isn’t ideal at this age. It would be helpful if the aquarium provided platforms or better visibility for younger visitors.

We also found it disappointing that we couldn’t choose the backgrounds for our souvenir photos. The staff selected them for us, and they didn’t match our preferences. Given the price of the photos, guests should be allowed to decide how they want their memories to look.

Lastly, the staff handing out the photos at the exit could benefit from more politeness and patience. Unfortunately, this interaction left a rather negative impression at the end of an otherwise fun visit.

editorial_summary.overview: Local theatre space in a former shed, offering drama and music performances and kids' shows.

result.formatted_address: 290 Chase Side, London N14 4PE, UK
result.name: Chickenshed

reviews.text:
Once inside you come through double doors that open and can follow the footsteps on the floor which will guide you inside. Staff are friendly and welcoming. The space is clean, spacious and brightly lit. The colour chairs and tables add some character into the waiting space and the spot lights across the ceiling help build the environment. Such a great place that is not too far from the Oakwood station, it was actually a nice stroll maybe 10-12 minutes away on a straight road. Beside them is a small park with a playground and the cherry blossom trees which are in full bloom at the moment. They do have a cafe here so you can have a hot cuppa before or after the show. Everything is one level which means it’s buggy/stroller accessible. The team gave out stickers when we entered which nice.

The show is fantastic full of energy, live narration, vocals singing and dancing. My little one kept dancing and touching the puppets. All of the character were fun and colorful. The entire crew were so happy and energetic always making eye contact with everyone in the crowd and getting the kids to dance with all of their body. They even teach you sign languages which is great. As an adult I could see why this show was so popular and they always encouraged children to come to the stage and get involved. Lots of dancing positive vibes. I think this may have been the best children’s show I have been to so far and I would 100% go again. I also love how everyone is in Matt’s in the floor and were able to really see and hear everyone in the show.

You can even purchase merchandise and support by becoming a friend of Chickenshed. Overall the space is very organized, clean and fun I would recommend to friends and family and I would come back in future for other shows. Not to forget to mention the beautiful outdoor space that they have in the side which is open during the summer. The lights on top make it feel like a magical space for the children to enjoy.

We did join the first stay and play session they had one for £3 per child, it had colouring, drums, hula hoops, shapes to play with the light and shadow, foam squares and headband wear. The team are full of energy and enthusiasm. They really enjoy playing with children and encouraging them to join in.
Totally Tales was brilliant and thoroughly enjoyed by my grandchildren. So inclusive to all children each one made to feel special. Thank you. Marion Firth x

I love Chickenshed! Best theatre and incredible ethos. They've been accepting everyone and adapting naturally for over 50 years to ensure anyone can participate and shine. Their December musical shows are as good or better than any I've seen in the West End. Full of heart! And bucketloads of talent 💗

Fantastic afternoon watching 'Rush' based on the Windrush scandal. Absolutely brilliant performances from everyone involved. Such an inclusive production. Outstanding dancing and singing. Very well produced. Will be supporting this theatre and their work more in the future.

Chicken shed has some great Christmas shows of of all time, but some of the new ones they do are not that great apart from Peter Pan what’s the greatest Christmas show I’ve seen last year last year chicken is all exclusive chicken shed theatre has one of the best shows I’ve been to see Summer shows at chicken shed, not one of the best I have seen at chicken shed theatre The greatest building I’ve been to, I was the eighth of seven been there throughout my experience at chicken head age of seven as a child it was a trip of a lifetime being at chicken shed theatre, I’ve been to chicken head cause you might foundation degree and my BTEC course but I didn’t finish the course I didn’t finish the course because of Covid fancy some shows, but only the Christmas shows are the best shows I’ve performed with chicken yet but my first Christmas show and I did was Pinocchio I had my big break doing Night before Christmas I had a tiny part in a Christmas Carol been performing with chicken shed a long time now many years with a great experience for me paying that chicken shed theatre

editorial_summary.overview: A vast treasury of science & invention, famous for its state-of-the-art interactive exhibits.

result.name: Science Museum

reviews.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ ✈️ 💊 🩺🩻🚀

The Science Museum is a fantastic place to spend the day! A true humbling experience of the world of science

The exhibits are interactive, fun, and packed with fascinating information perfect for both kids and adults. I especially loved how hands on so many of the displays are; it makes learning feel exciting and engaging rather than just reading from a plaque.

The museum covers such a wide range of topics, from space and engineering to medicine and technology, so there’s truly something for everyone. The staff are welcoming and knowledgeable, and the layout makes it easy to explore without feeling overwhelmed.

It’s inspiring to see science brought to life in such an accessible way. Whether you’re visiting with family, friends, or even solo, the Science Museum is an absolute must-visit.

Definitely worth a visit at least once! The museum has so many fascinating exhibits, so plan to spend plenty of time if you want to see everything. It’s a great place to learn about science—whether it’s how the human body works or the history of the steam train. Kids can explore, play, and learn in a very hands-on way, which makes it even more engaging.
Not to mention that all staff was cool and friendly.

There are dining areas and some lovely gift shops to enjoy as well. Tickets can be purchased online in advance, or directly at the entrance on the day of your visit.

The Science Museum is such a fun and interesting place to visit! There’s so much to see and do for all ages—from space rockets and historic inventions to hands-on experiments and interactive zones for kids. We don’t have anything like this in Toronto, so it was a real treat to explore. It’s free to enter (some exhibits cost extra), and you can easily spend hours here. Definitely a must-visit if you’re in London!

The Science Museum in London is truly amazing! If you believe in the power of science and admire its wonders, this place is a must-visit. Especially for children, it's both educational and incredibly fun. There are interactive exhibits, space technology displays, engineering marvels, and so much more. Your kids should absolutely see and experience it firsthand. I spent hours exploring and loved every moment — each floor offers a different world. A must for anyone who loves science.

A fantastic museum, especially for children! There’s so much to explore — interactive exhibits, current topics, and lots of opportunities to learn and be inspired.

Museums like this are essential: they help the younger generation grow, dream, and imagine a better world, while adults can remember history and support children’s curiosity. Highly recommended for families and anyone interested in science and discovery!

editorial_summary.overview: Traditional Victorian theatre hosting large-scale productions aimed at new audiences.

result.formatted_address: Gerry Raffles Square, Theatre Square, London E15 1BN, UK
result.name: Stratford East

reviews.text: Visited Stratford East to watch the musical The Harder They Come - the production was phenomenal! Highly recommend you visit the show while it's still on. Be quick, seats are selling quickly! Easy to access the building, there wasn't a long wait to get in. Staff were helpful. Area is well lit and has some parking spaces - first come, first served! Easy transport links to the area too. Plus suitable stopping space for Ubers to collect passengers.

Honestly, what a lovely concept and it’s so nicely tucked away in Stratford. Absolutely love how they have something for everyone, lots of games, drinks and food.
I’m still to come see a movie here but I can’t wait to come back.

It’s a lovely space to spend a weekend evening with friends

Lovely theatre with interesting productions. Female toilet situation is frustrating though - no toilet paper in majority of cubicles during interval and at end of show. Such an organised venue should pre-plan for the busiest moments or at least leave spare rolls in the cubicles.
A gem of a theatre in Stratford. Shows are excellent and well priced. Great food at the venue and also a Sichuan restaurant next door.

I haven't been in 'The Theatre Royal' (as I knew it) since either my childhood or bringing my daughter to see Aladdin years ago.
I was here to watch Love Stuck.  It was funny what I saw that is.
Unfortunately, the show had to be cancelled.  One of the actors was taken ill.  The lead lady was already the understudy.  I've rebooked for the 4th of July.
The seats I originally had were good.  I was in the stalls row K. I'm booked for the 3rd row next time.  Obviously, I didn't have to pay for the rebooking.
I was a bit shocked by the cost of the drinks.  I ordered two double gin and tonics and it was £24.
A good trip down memory lane.  I met some lovely ladies last week too.

editorial_summary.overview: Victorian school museum in converted warehouse with replica classroom and interactive activities.

result.formatted_address: 46-50 Copperfield Rd, canal side, London E3 4RR, UK
result.name: Ragged School Museum

reviews.text: I wasn't sure what to expect before I went but I'm so glad I visited. My Nan attended this school from late 1889 to early 1892. It was amazing to stand in the very room where she would have been taught. The reconstructed classroom is excellent and the school group that were visiting while I was there seemed to enjoy being taught the "Victorian way" by an actress playing the part of a schoolmistress. The exhibits and information about the Ragged School Movement is very interesting and isn't too overwhelming in content. There is also a reconstruction of a typical house from the Victorian era. It's difficult to imagine how families lived in such conditions. I thoroughly recommend this museum. It's well worth the modest entry fee.

A hidden gem that deserves a lot more exposure as it highlights just how tragic life was for Victorian parents who couldn't afford education for their children, and how the concept of Ragged School sought to correct this gap for the thousands of impoverished kids living in London. There's an entire classroom that gives you an idea of how basic the day to day learning was and it's actually used even now to give kids today an idea of just how simple the classrooms back then really were. There's also a room above the classroom that paints a picture of what extreme poverty looked like in Victorian London and it makes for a sombre experience. Definitely a museum that's under the radar but one that you should check out to learn just how tragically difficult it was for Victorian children to have an education - a tool that by right should be universal for all, no matter who you are or where you're from.

Great experience my 6 year old who loved it. We attended the Victorian classroom which is every 1st Sunday of the month. We combined it with a walk down the canal and some playtime in Mile end park. You wouldn’t more than two hours there. There’s parking available on the weekends on the street.

What a great museum. We enjoyed reading all the information about the school and the children that attended. And really loved the classroom and being able to sit at the desks. It's fascinating to see how life was during that period. Well worth visiting.

Visited on a bright sunny morning - it’s a great place right between the park and the canal. The cafe is a lovely spot for a coffee and a fab selection of cakes. The museum has some very interesting displays with historic information and the Victorian classroom experience was fantastic!!

editorial_summary.overview: Toys, clothes and interactives in 1872 hangar with marble floor and visible cast iron skeleton.

result.formatted_address: Cambridge Heath Rd, Bethnal Green, London E2 9PA, UK
result.name: Young V&A

reviews.text: A lovely museum. Most people visit with children, but don’t let that stop you if you’re there as a big kid. Plenty of things to take you down memory lane and jog your memory of your childhood. And if all else fails, the architecture of their beautiful building is gorgeous with its delicate steel/iron work.

Free museum. Went on a weekend. Moderate crowd. No lining up or booking required. Just walk in. Very accessible galleries. Kids 12, 10 and 3 enjoyed themselves - lots of stiff catering to different developmental ages. There's outdoor activities on selected days too - just staff entertaining the kids and parents. All round fun.

It's a great place to visit with kids and toddlers. My little one loved every moment of it. There's ample space for strollers, and the cafe inside is a wonderful addition too. Overall, it's a fantastic place for not only kids but adults as well!

Tickets are not required unless it has an exhibition within the Young V&A. In this case it was the Egyptian Exhibition. My 6yo daughter was free but I paid 10quid for a ticket. The ticket grants multiple entries (no further payment required) into the exhibition until it ends. So it worth it! My daughter and I enjoyed the exhibition in addition to the multiple rooms in the Young V&A itself. It was interactive with plenty of activities such as puzzles, information films, role plays and games. It's a place we'll be returning to until my daughter has grown out of it

Recently opened after refurbishment, this is an interactive museum that would be a joy to visit for both children and adults.

Visited the Making Egypt exhibition and absolutely loved it: well curated, clear explanations and very relatable. Highly recommended!

Has a special space for under two-s, a fun sand-play area and a dollhouse section.

editorial_summary.overview: Performances and participatory events at UK's leading theatre for audiences aged 2-21 years.

result.formatted_address: 147 Tooley St, London SE1 2HZ, UK
result.name: Unicorn Theatre

reviews.text: Great little theatre close to London Bridge. Comfortable seats. Recommend row A in the stalls for the best view. Watched 'The Koala who could' which was a nice funny production. Kid loved it (had to buy the book after which they were selling)  She looks forward to coming back for another production Staff professional and friendly.

We managed to see Pig Heart Boy, a Malorie Blackman adaptation, and what a fantastic production it was. My daughter had read the book and seen the film, so it was great to add the play to the list. The theatre is a nice intimate size, but finding the seats in the D shaped area wasn't easy. They are essentially benches with numbers that arent easy to see. There is plenty of legroom and because of the bench style seating, plenty of seating space and sitting second row from the front gave us a perfect view.

Great for Children! The crowd is always involved in the plays at some point, which the children love. Very relaxed setting...

Lovely location too.. Perfect for a meal or walk by the river with great views and pictures of tower bridge...

Unicorn — Bold, Funny, and Uncomfortably Honest Mike Bartlett’s Unicorn, now playing at the Garrick Theatre, is a provocative deep-dive into modern relationships, polyamory, and the quiet desperation of middle-aged marriage. With a cast led by Nicola Walker, Stephen Mangan, and Erin Doherty, the play balances sharp wit with emotional nuance.

Plot Snapshot: Polly and Nick, a married couple stuck in a rut, invite Polly’s younger student Kate into their relationship — not just for sex, but as a potential third partner. What unfolds is a mix of awkward comedy, raw vulnerability, and philosophical musings on love, honesty, and change.

Amazing! First visit there and watched Home Song! A production that definitely brought it home... Goosebumps occurred with beautiful storytelling, singing, interaction and play. My toddler now as 'Ghana' 🇬🇭 As part of her vocabulary and was SUCH for her to connect with her heritage in London through the Arts!

editorial_summary.overview: Long-running theatre staging classic & modern productions, many with well known actors & directors.

result.formatted_address: 103 The Cut, London SE1 8NB, UK
result.name: The Old Vic

reviews.text: First visit to the Old Vic and we thoroughly enjoyed it. Great view of the stage from our seats and good sound quality too. Easy to get to the bar and plenty of water jugs/glasses available for those that would rather just rehydrate. Toilets easily accessible and no real queues considering the show was a sell out. Would definitely recommend and we will be back.

Great venue & seen Mary Page Marlowe is a deeply moving piece of theatre — intelligent, compassionate, and brave in its refusal to simplify. Susan Sarandon and Andrea Riseborough anchor the production powerfully, while the ensemble and design amplify the emotional resonance. This is a play that lingers long after you leave: not because it ends with a dramatic finale, but because life itself — messy, unplanned, beautiful — still pulses in its echo.

If you have the chance, it’s very much worth seeing.

Called in here for a coffee and to find out more about The Old Vic. It's just around the corner from Waterloo station.
The Cut is a wonderful area with really nice restaurants cafes and shops ,
it has a nice vibe.
There is also The Young Vic which I had no idea about just down the road.
I will be keeping an eye on what's on in these theatres in future.
The staff at The Old Vic were very welcoming.
The café inside is well worth a visit.

Fabulous theatre! Staff are super attentive too, I had an issue where I was sat and the ushers were quick to help me resolve it. Plenty of loos - love that they’re gender inclusive. Price of merchandise is really affordable too compared to other theatres. The box office staff are really helpful, allowed me to exchange a ticket for credit voucher

I didn’t care for this particular play but the venue is excellent.
There’s really no awful seats. I think 🤔 that you would have a good view from anywhere, other than maybe the top floor. (I’ve never bought seats up there)
Every floor has a concession with a seating area. (Not the main entrance) The seats are comfortable with plenty of leg room. The sound system is good and it’s easy to hear what’s being said.

Took the kids swimming here for the first time in some years, as they used to love it. It has been ruined. Won't take the kids swimming here again.

Queue outside in the rain, let in 5 minutes before the start of the session, which is only an hour long.

Water freezing. Flume closed. Lazy river switched off. Two wave sessions in one hour. Poolside shower freezing cold. Broken showers in the changing rooms. My two year olds didn't last the hour as it was freezing. My 5 and 7 year olds obviously wanted more than an hour.

Awful, awful, awful.

The gym is falling to pieces. A lot of equipment is in bad conditions, and some equipment is missing!

result.name: Abbey Leisure Centre

reviews.text: This gym is absolutely disgusting. Gym floor, bathrooms, showers, and the swimming pool are all very dirty places. I used to be a member before the refurbishment and after, and to be honest nothing has changed (apart of the equipement and the gym layout obviously)  Always some paper, chewing gums, plasters and even nails on the floor. Pictures and the videos are from 2 days only. But it is always like that, or even worse.

very helpful tour given by Brad today, the gym looks great i was really impressed by their reformer studio, the cardio machines are amazing too giving you POV while you work out, facilities has definitely improved. The price is definitely worth it compared to what local gyms in the area offer.

The staff is entitled and some of them are borderline racist as well. reviews.text:
Copthall Leisure Centre has its strengths, but also some areas that really need improvement.

Starting with the gym – it’s a decent size and has a good range of equipment, but it’s consistently overcrowded, especially during peak hours. Unfortunately, poor ventilation makes the space feel stuffy and uncomfortable, especially during intense workouts. It definitely could use better airflow or air conditioning.

On a more positive note, the swimming facilities are excellent. The pools are well-maintained and the swimming classes are top-notch. The coaches are experienced and friendly, and there’s a wide variety of intensive classes that cater to all levels – this is easily the best part of the centre.

The café is okay – not spectacular, but it does the job. They offer a solid selection of protein shakes, which is great post-workout, though the rest of the menu could be a bit more exciting.

Overall, Copthall Leisure Centre has potential. If they improve the ventilation and manage gym crowding better, it could be a much more enjoyable place to train.

One of the worst experiences I’ve had at a leisure centre in the UK.

Upon arrival, we had to queue for about 5 minutes at reception. The receptionist specifically told me to go to the competition pool after I showed him my mobile booking. When we got there, we were told to go to the community pool because there was a lesson taking place. At the community pool, we were redirected AGAIN —this time to the learner pool, because another lesson was running. That’s ridiculous—I paid for the competition pool but ended up in the learner pool!

After about 15 minutes, a staff member came over and told me we could now go to the competition pool as the lesson had overrun. What a JOKE! It honestly felt like we were being messed around the entire time.

By the time we finally got in, we only had about 20 minutes left before 11:50 a.m. On top of that, we were told we could only swim in a restricted area, since the rest of the pool wasn’t suitable for children who couldn’t manage the deep end. That left us confined to a tiny 6 x 12.5 metre SECTION!!!

My only advice: think twice before planning a visit here. Don’t get me wrong—the facilities themselves are fantastic—but the management is absolutely TERRIBLE!!!

Today I had the pleasure of being assisted by a lovely and professional young lady called Lamia. I was amazed at the way she was able to help me without making me feel rushed and flustered. She was very respectful and help everyone in a polite manner. Coptall needs more of Lamia....

My experience of Copthall gym has been very positive since joining  it a couple of months ago. The staff are very helpful and friendly. In particular, Lamia has been excellent in promptly resolving a few parking issues I had since joining the gym.

Good clean gym, fairly well equipped and most equipment is new and well looked after, good pricing, can be super busy dependant on what time you go so watch out! Couple of the PTs are a bit entitled and think they can reserve equipment / space for their clients like it’s more important than YOUR workout though so beware of that too.

The hall that the reception desk opens into is speckled with different table games.
The gym has got a host of equipment that can be utilised by adults and children(with age suitability)
The outside space has got typical garden tables/chairs or even benches and a small wooden stage to hold small events. It must be a treat in the summers(You are allowed to use the space in winters too if you are adventurous) .The roof top pitch is icing on the cake nestled within netting all over to avoid any balls going astray.
In many places the hard work of the children is also reflected. They have themselves decorated and painted the walls of different rooms to their own sensibility(aided and supervised by their tutors, instructors and coaches)
There is a small cosy library caters to the book lovers. The children have the regular support of English and Maths Tutors too if required.
In short, the place is remarkable. An epitome of excellence. You pay £5 for an Annual membership and 50p for the activities.
It is a fairly new establishment.(started in 2019) but has seen the onslaught of the pandemic. However following the Government guidelines, they have operated when advised. I think the success of such places owes to the interest of the locals. There is SO MUCH MORE than you could see from outside or even hear. Better experience it first hand.
I have had the opportunity of meeting the personnel and can assure you that they are sincere to the cause of promoting wellness , Health and Inclusion of the Community. Do join and commit yourselves to some productive use of your leisure time.

reviews.text:
Although we've been many times to this beautiful park, today was the first time we hired recumbent bikes (banana bikes) and it was absolutely brilliant! My two daughters (9 and 6) took to them straightaway, although the younger one struggled initially with the steering.

They both said it was fantastic fun and we're already planning another visit of the next few weeks.

DEFINITELY recommend!

Great setup and no fuss whatsoever. Fun for all the family or friends. Do make sure you check what is available as there is a number of different bikes to choose from.

The sit down bikes we had are hard work, but fun and the trike for my daughter was great for her. You get 1 hour which will get you a few laps round the park.

Get there early, the afternoons can get busy.

An easy walk from Battersea Power Station and a great experience to do with children. The roads in the park are wide and flat, and three different sizes of recumbent bikes can be hired depending on age of your kids (plus they also have normal bikes, trikes and a bike with a “bucket seat” on the front into which smaller children can be strapped in). The cost is £17 per hour (per bike!) but on the day we visited they were not very busy so we were given an extra 20 mins for free. The staff are super helpful and can adjust bikes in the blink of an eye and answer all of your questions, we even changed one of ours after 10 mins for a bigger size and nothing was too much of a problem. They will look after bags too if needed. The rest of Battersea Park is also amazing; there is an excellent (free!) playground with huge slides, a zip wire and mini outdoor trampolines at the other end of the park next to the (paid for) Go Ape treetop facility. Plenty of toilets and tea / coffee / ice cream places in park too and lots of wide open green spaces for ball games too, so you can easily make a day out of it.

We rented a Robin bike and banana bikes for children and adults during half term. The staff were so lovely  and gracious. They were great with instructions, helping set up the bikes and changing them when my niece couldn’t use the banana bike. Would highly recommend the company and hiring of the bikes for some good fun & semi fitness!.
I rented a bike from this office and the service was excellent. Special thanks to Marten for the great support and friendliness.

I am writing to express my deep disappointment regarding my experience with your gym. I had been a member from November 2024 until I decided to cancel my membership in April 2025. The gym's location is very convenient for me, as it is close to my home, and I genuinely enjoyed working out there.

However, one of the main issues that led to my cancellation was the gym's early closing time. Many residents in the area, including myself, work late and prefer to visit the gym around 9:00 to 9:30 PM. Unfortunately, although the gym is advertised to be open until 10:00 PM, access is effectively restricted from 9:30 PM onwards.

On one occasion, I arrived at the gym after work only to find the front door locked at 9:30 PM. I waited outside until someone exited so I could enter. When I spoke to a staff member about it, I was met with rudeness and was told the gym was closed—even though it was only 9:35 PM. I explained that there were still 25 minutes remaining, but she responded harshly and unprofessionally.

Additionally, it has become routine for staff to begin ushering members out from 9:30 PM onwards, often raising their voices, which disrupts the workout environment. As paying members, we expect access until the stated closing time of 10:00 PM.

Moreover, the gym was closed for an entire week in December, including from December 24th to January 6th, without any notice on the website or proper communication. Despite these closures, we were still charged the full membership fee, which I find unacceptable.

Due to these ongoing issues and lack of transparency, I chose to cancel my membership. It’s disappointing because this gym has the potential to be a great facility for the local community. I sincerely hope that another gym opens in the RM8 area to provide better service and break the current monopoly.

We had a confirmed badminton court booking through the Better UK App — with a confirmation email to prove it. But when we arrived, we were told the court had been “booked by someone else” due to a system error, and we were forcibly kicked out by an incredibly rude and aggressive manager.

Instead of helping resolve the situation, the manager dismissed our confirmation, refused to listen, talked over us the entire time, and repeatedly told us to leave. His tone and behavior were not only deeply unprofessional, but downright hostile. It was clear he had no intention of treating us with fairness or respect.

We strongly suspect that racial discrimination played a role in how we were treated. We were not given the courtesy of a conversation, just immediately blamed and removed — despite having proof of our booking.

The gym’s layout is another major downside. One section is always overcrowded, while other areas remain practically empty. This poor design isn’t just inconvenient; it’s also unsafe. Equipment is placed too close together, creating a risk of injury. Whoever planned the setup clearly didn’t consider functionality or safety.

On the positive side, the natural light is fantastic. The large windows fill the space with daylight, creating a more pleasant environment. Additionally, the gym has plenty of new equipment, which is a definite plus. The swimming facilities are also a nice bonus for those who enjoy using them.

However, cleanliness is a significant issue, particularly in the men’s toilets. They are consistently dirty, and the smell is unbearable. For a facility charging full price, this level of hygiene is unacceptable.

Overall, this gym might be worth it if you qualify for a discount (e.g., for unemployment or disability). But at full price, there are better and more affordable options nearby.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ | Riverside Leisure Centre: More Than Just an Ice Rink (But Good Luck With the Vending Machines)

Ah, Riverside Leisure Centre - where I spend so much time, I may as well set up a bed in the corner. My daughter plays ice hockey here, and compared to some of the horrifying ice rinks we travel to for matches (see my other scathing reviews for tales of tragic toilets), this place is actually really good.

The facilities are great - at least, I assume they are, since most of them are closed by the time training kicks off at 9:45 PM. Want a post-practice snack? Hope you like the thrill of gambling with a vending machine that’s either empty, broken, or requires a PhD to operate. I often find myself coaching a group of confused teenagers from the Friday night disco skate (think nightclub on ice - smoke machines, chaos, and teens with questionable balance) on how to work the thing. If only they’d put me on payroll.

The ice? Solid. Seating? Decent. The PA system? A complete mystery. Match announcements sound like they’re being transmitted from a WW2 bunker - muffled, garbled, and completely unintelligible. But hey, it adds to the drama.

Oh, and parking? I haven’t paid in three years, so I’m assuming it’s free. Or I’m on the run from some serious fines. Either way, bonus!

Would I recommend? Definitely. Just bring snacks and don’t rely on the PA system to know what’s going on.

2. Health Hazards Everywhere

Air conditioning has been out of service for months — turning the downstairs gym into a sauna. People have reported nearly fainting from the heat. In summer, showers are infested with mould, flies, and an overpowering stench of body odour. Temperature regulation in the showers swings from ice cold to scalding with no control, and the place reeks of neglect.

3. Staff & Management Issues

Multiple users report that management is dismissive, unprofessional, and even rude when approached with genuine concerns. Some staff members appear more focused on watching gym-goers than helping them, making the atmosphere tense and unwelcoming.

Bottom Line: This centre needs urgent intervention from the local council or regulatory health authorities. If you care about your health, safety, and money — avoid this place entirely. You’re better off training elsewhere until this facility undergoes a serious overhaul.

Situated inside Mayesbrook Park, this centre comprises of a large hall which is divided in half, with one section set up as a trampoline jump park and the other as a regular sports hall, which can be used for a battery of activities.

The centre is accessible, with step-free access, lifts and accessible toilets, but the trampoline area is not.

There is a café on the first floor which sells a range of hot and cold drinks, snacks and sandwiches, all at the prices you’d expect for this sort of place. Card payment only, which annoys me, but won’t bother most people.

Staff are friendly and helpful and the centre is fairly clean and tidy throughout.

If you get a hot drink, ask to put your own milk in - I ended up with the most disgustingly milky cup of tea!

Good fun for kids and pretty good value at £10 per person for an hour long session.

Plenty of parking available too, which is free.

Cordell was an exceptional party host. He was very accommodating and made our children’s party amazing. I would highly recommend anyone wanting to throw a trampolining party because of his efforts. Thank you so much!!

I paid over £3 for a coffee that was truly unacceptable: practically just foam, with no taste or body. This is not what you would expect from a place charging these prices. The staff urgently need proper training, because the current standard is far below expectations. The kindness of the staff does not make up for the complete lack of quality in the product served.

The gym itself is probably the best Better gym i have ever been to with all the facilities they have. The staff are very good, particularly  Sammy who taught a spin class which I attended for the very first time and he was an excellent teacher that paced the session well and kept it entertaining as well as challenging, would definitely recommend his classes and the gym as a whole.

reviews.text:
The staff are great and the gym is good but the recent change to their entry gate system has been a nightmare. I have to get a staff member to let me through about half the time as the gates and the app aren't working as they should.

Pool is good but the public are often crammed into two lanes to accommodate for swimming lessons. This can sometimes be made more frustrating by the fact that the lessons are not always taking place in all of the designated lanes at the time.

Arrived early for the first swim with my young primary school aged daughter, who had a swimming competition later in the day and felt nervous about her backstroke, poor thing, but we've all been there with nerves.

We paid a stonking £9 for her to swim (I wasn't going in). However, the pool was packed. There were three people in each lane, every lane. 8.10 in the morning! I'd say the vast majority were older than 40 or 50, though it can be hard to tell. Of course there were lanes of various speed, but my daughter was going to be swimming the 25 metres in less than 20 seconds, she would quite clearly have had to slow down (therefore not preparing for the competition) or just steaming through and colliding with the person in front. That wouldn't work for anyone. She hadn't even gone in, so I politely asked for a refund for her. The swim manager said no as she could join a lane as the fourth person. Yes, of course she could in theory, but in practice it wouldn't work. The manager still insisted no, it wasn't possible. He went to walk off, as he did I asked him his name (I won't write it here) and asked whether anyone had ever done him a favour, you know let him off. He looked at me sheepishly and said yes, they had, but he wasn't going to do us a favour in this instance because he'd have to explain the refund to his boss and he didn't want to go through that.

Honestly,  the pool was jam packed, they didn't look like they needed our £9. I thanked him for his time and left with my daughter to Northolt pool, just a ten minute drive away. £2.60 for her swim and a lane to herself! And she achieved the sub-20 seconds in the race a few hours ago, no thanks to Highgrove Pool.

Honestly guys, this was so mean. A child wanting to practice swimming for a competition, making no fuss, just asking for her £9 refund, and you couldn't do it?!

The lady at reception was lovely, and she had inspired me to join the pool at £40 for adult membership and £23 each for my 3 children as the pool is so local and convenient to us. Doing the maths that would have been £1308 per year. Lost over 9 quid!

Equipment is fine if you can actually get on to use it. Every single time I come here there is always 10 years olds running around taking up machine to muck about. No idea why unattended kids are allowed to run around the gym when PAYING members are trying to work out. Other gym members are clearly annoyed by the fact they have to share a gym with the after school club - it’s unacceptable and clearly everyone agrees!

reviews.text:
🏸  Booked courts for badminton expecting to have a good session. However that wasn't the case, the lights are so bright above courts it's impossible to hit the shuttles without blinding yourself. The nets obstruct your walkway with barriers still placed at some places (leaks observed). Interfering with courts.

Few people mentioned the courts aren't cleaned or maintained properly. With one court having a damaged corner on the ground that they failed at trying to fix. Also poses a health and safety risk. Serious concerns, over slips, trips and falls hazard. It's just a disaster to pay FULL price for this court an these are the standards from a "Sports Centre" my goodness. I'd be shocked to see the other courts honestly. John Warner himself wouldn't be impressed.

Good value membership. I especially enjoy my yoga class; Lauren is an excellent instructor. She is kind, encouraging and adapts the class to account for all ages and abilities. The sound of her voice relaxes me straightaway. Thank you Lauren for doing a great job.

What a great place.
Been using facilities here for the past 6 months, started taking our grandchildren to swimming and softplay, Staff friendly and professional, always made to feel welcome. Cafe, priced well, good variety of food for both children and adults, and vegetarian options,, lovely atmosphere and filtered air-conditioning.
Highly recommend, met some great people, also joining gym and swimming will update.
I use it for the swimming pool part and it is great. However it is very convenient with all other sports, gym and even soft play with café. Always parking space and very easy place to drive too.

*Soft play* It is an affordable day out when the weather is grey and cold but this soft play feels a bit sad and dated. Some of the items are damaged( ripped with foam being exposed), there is no ball pit! I have never been to a soft play with no ball pit. Under 1's go for £1.90 so it is a great price but could do with some more excitement. Also the cafe upstairs seems to be closed? We go weekly as a group and never see any stuff managing it.

editorial_summary.overview: Unpretentious gym with machines, fitness classes, 2 pools & a hall for football & net sports.

reviews.text: Staff here seem nice, lots of parking, nice location, good centre... but the price!?! Swimming is a life skill, we have to teach our children to swim, how is it acceptable to charge £25 for 1 hour of swimming?!?! I decided to use a different well known company and the cost was significantly cheaper - more than £15 cheaper! The centre and the staff are nice, but the price is shocking.

Absolutely rip off this gym! Not only do you pay for memebership per month which is already expensive, but when you book the classes on the app and you don’t cancel within the 4 hour time slot they charge you and you need to clear off that payment before booking another class online. This is the only gym where they charge you extra for classes although paying for membership. They sent me an email twice saying I was a no show when I attended the class and they said the barriers at the reception when I scanned my card was not working, sort it out before charging people for your mistakes and emailing.

i love the gym. it’s gorgeous and big. the rest of the leisure is centre is amazing too.

gym is just constantly busy, there is always too many - ruins my whole workout. even going during non peak times - it’s still too busy.

I use the gym on a pay as you go basis. It's always easy to book and pay online and if you have any issues the staff at the centre are helpful and friendly. There's a good range of equipment and it's clean and in good condition. Changing rooms are clean too. I think that it's good value

I had my sons 7th birthday party in the small pool last Saturday, and I highly recommend it. The whole experience from start to finish was faultless, the changing rooms was separate, we had a key for each to leave our stuff, a lifeguard watching the pool, a great member of staff in the pool, Jake was brilliant, he led the kids, he entertained with games, which was fun. There wasn’t many adults that wanted to get in originally until they saw it and we ended up with more than enough adults.
The ends part that Jake did with the happy birthday was out of this world.
We then went to have the food in the cafeteria and Tracy went above and beyond to ensure it worked out perfectly, every detail from the lights being switched off for happy birthday to the cake being cut!

editorial_summary.overview: Huge complex offering indoor & outdoor sports courts, a boxing gym & a fitness centre.

reviews.text: Great experience at this place, I took my 4 year old sister and we went to the inflatable park and she absolutely loved it!! The staff were also friendly especially Christopher and Naweed, big up them for their great customer service inside the venue and allowing our experience to be great!

The best softplay / multi active zone. So much to do, so clean, equipped, well lit, overall a fantastic fun filled experience today. Polite helpful staff. My son loved it so much that we had to book an additional hour!!! Recommended highly. Just amazing 🤩

This place is excellent ! So many good things to play with for kids age 6 months to 11 years +
The have trampoline, bouncing castle with slides , soft play for toddler and kids separated .
Car park is separated and payable with ringo . Watch out for the warrens who will come 5 min before the end time

We love love love this place. Whether you live far or close this is a great place for your little ones. Firstly you can bring your buggy/prams as they have a place for you to park it, secondly you should buy your tickets online to save time and thirdly bring plenty of water as you will need it. I went here with my toddler and she loves it. They have a huge space dedicated to the giant jungle gym where you can either play in the under 2’s area or where all the other older kids go. This is adult friendly and strong enough for you to also enjoy and bring out your inner kid. After 10 minutes I was already sweating and felt like this was PE all over again. If can get very busy as we saw multiple birthdays parties here booked into different time slots. Depending on when you book you will be given a coloured paper wrist band on your child’s wrist that determines the time for you leave. The allocated time slot is definitely enough time for your little ones to work up a sweat and for you to leave with them ready for nap time. Highly recommend this place to all parents who want a nice day out that won’t break the bank and has clean changing facilities in multiple toilets so even if you have to wait it won’t be for too long. They also have a cafe on site so you can refresh with sweet treats and even a refreshing slushy. We came here by guys and it was easily accessible with the buggy and easy to find.
Heads up parents you should be dressed comfortably as you too will be moving around and  climbing, jumping and rolling around.

Great place to visit with the kids !
Soft play area for under 10’s, indoor zip line, inflatables, trampolines & plenty of other games and activities to do for hours.

result.formatted_address: 4 Edensor Rd, Chiswick, London W4 2RG, UK
result.name: New Chiswick Pool

reviews.text:
The new Chiswick Pool is a well-maintained facility with good amenities, but it doesn’t offer enough time for lane swimming, especially for adults who work standard hours. The schedule is heavily geared towards schools and clubs, which limits public access during the day. While there are some early morning and late evening slots, these aren’t always convenient for everyone.

The pool itself is clean, and the staff are friendly, but the lack of flexible lane swimming times makes it less accessible for the wider community. If you’re looking for a pool where you can regularly swim at convenient hours, this might not be the best option. It would be great if they could balance the timetable to better accommodate working adults.
Update to previous review

Trying to get my money refunded from Chiswick Pool has been an absolute nightmare. What should have been a simple, straightforward process has turned into weeks of back-and-forth with no clear answers. I’ve been passed from one person to another, given vague promises, and left completely in the dark. The lack of communication and accountability is beyond frustrating. I expected better service, but honestly, it feels like they hope you’ll give up chasing your own money. Very disappointing experience.
It's getting abit tired and could do with a refurbishment.. its good value and popular with the locals. The council needs to invest more in such places that offer so much..staff are brilliant

Visited today with my 2 girls, seems they have changed the shower door which look new and clean, but the doors are without locks . The changing room could have cleaned more frequent as the floor was too wet, don’t seems to have any cleaner to clean regularly

The hair dryer area was a bit dirty as well

Good swimming pool & facilities for the price/public pool standards.
But let down by an inept/inconsiderate management who treat ordinary members/swimmers as third class users as schools / swimming lessons or others take precedence.
Meaning lanes are arbitrary closed off for ordinary public use to give more favoured swimmers the right to use them. Even once these more favoured swimmers have vacated their privileged lanes, the staff show little interest re-opening them for ordinary public use.

You aren't allowed in the pool at the weekend, unless it's between 8-9am. At 9am, staff kick everyone out so the pool can be used be families with kids for the rest of the day. How is this fair? Especially to members who are paying for full membership. You can imagine how packed out the pool gets between 8 and 9am because of this unfair rule. During my last visit, I had to leave the pool after 10 minutes because there were 8 people in my lane, all swimming at different speeds, which made it impossible to swim properly. It's also a health and safety hazard, but staff don't seem to care about overcrowding.

I think management should be more considerate of the fact not all of us work from home, or live near the pool, so weekend swimming is the only feasible option for some pool users.

reviews.text: A nice communal venue. Gym and pool are of reasonable upkeep.  My main concerns are the changing room floors get very dirty and slippery at times. I can recommend the café. Staff are friendly and helpful. The food and drink are reasonably priced too. Well worth just a social visit.

Really bad gym. Poor equipment and facilities. Changing room is in a state. Lockers with a note for longer than 2 years now, broken doors, sink without hand soap…  water fountains broken and nobody seems to care. Gym machines not working for weeks too… but hey, pay £45 every month for this service. Made a formal complaint before but they simply don’t care. It’s a joke.

I’ve been very disappointed with my experience at Isleworth Leisure Centre. The general cleanliness is extremely poor — the changing rooms are always dirty and in a state that suggests they are not cleaned regularly, if at all. This creates a really unpleasant environment for customers.

On top of that, the customer service is generally unhelpful. It’s nearly impossible to get anyone to answer the phone, and in-person support is often dismissive or uninterested.

One of the most frustrating aspects is the class booking system. If you miss a class without cancelling, your card is blocked — which is fair enough. However, the system still lets you pay for future classes without actually unblocking your card. So you arrive thinking everything is fine, only to find your card still doesn’t work and you're forced to pay again for the previous missed session. Essentially, you’re charged twice. That’s both poor system design and unfair to customers.

Given the poor standards of hygiene and unreliable service, this kind of policy just adds insult to injury. I’d seriously urge management to review both their facilities and their booking/payment processes.

Firstly, the changing rooms and showers absolutely stink, there’s no air so it smells of serious mould and all the times I’ve been, not once have I seen a cleaner on site. The pool is warm and doesn’t feel refreshing at all and the jacuzzi is always cold and once there were 2 men literally drinking champagne in plastic cups who stayed in there for an hour, it’s not some luxury spa? It’s a leisure centre. The jacuzzi is not even hot like how it’s suppose to be. Gym is basic and small, the personal trainers aren’t that bad but they don’t seem as qualified as personal trainers I’ve met in other gyms, nevertheless they show some enthusiasm. As for the customer service on reception, they have no interest and you can feel they don’t want to be there or help, they have no care in the world. Another thing to add is I’ve called this place on and off for the past year but I have never once been able to get through, the phone will ring forever. I cancelled my membership recently which was something I had been meaning to do for a while but my last straw was when I saw a family of 3 get in the pool fully clothed. I understand if you want to cover up but wear a wetsuit? Not leggings, long shirt or trackies? Come on this is unreal and inconsiderate to others, it put me off so much I had to get out the pool. Will never come back and I seriously wouldn’t recommend it to anyone.

Extremely Disappointing and Unsafe Experience

I feel compelled to leave this review after a truly poor visit to the swimming pool. The facility was dangerously overcrowded, with far too few lifeguards present to ensure safety. There was no challenge to boisterous or reckless behaviour—teenagers were throwing footballs the length of the pool with no regard for the safety of younger swimmers.

Play-fighting and rough behaviour were spilling into areas where small children were present, yet this went unchecked. Groups of teenage boys were intimidating and made the environment feel unsafe and unwelcoming for families and younger visitors.

Additionally, shoes were being worn poolside with no intervention from staff, and the floor, showers, and changing areas were filthy. Hygiene and safety standards were clearly not being maintained.

After just 15 minutes, we felt compelled to leave. This should have been a safe, enjoyable experience for all, but instead it was chaotic, unsupervised, and unacceptable. We will not be returning and hope management takes immediate action to improve staffing, cleanliness, and control within the facility.

The Gym franchise can charge just over £20 and you get the welcoming and helpful staff for free but Larkfield’s top tier of over £50 is somewhat extortionate for what you actually get but I suppose the toxic environment does come for free.

Clean around the pool areas, toilets clean and changing room areas. Showers were brilliant with hot water and great pressure. reviews.text: Nice place for kids to enjoy and play. Also, it is a very good arrangement to organise birthday parties. The only drawback is that it has a very small parking. I went there last Sunday and had to wait for a very long time to find a parking spot. The staff were very helpful and treated us very well. Overall, it was a nice place.

We recently hosted attended a birthday party at Oxygen Jumping in Acton, and while there were some positive aspects, the overall experience left much to be desired.

Parking and Accessibility: One of the most significant drawbacks was the parking situation. The lot is quite small, making it extremely challenging to find a spot, even if you’re willing to walk 15 minutes. The location feels isolated, which adds to the inconvenience.

Entry and Staff: Upon arrival, we encountered a lengthy waiting time to get inside. Once we finally made it in, we noticed that the staff seemed overwhelmed and not very attentive. It felt like they were stretched too thin to provide the level of service we expected.

Facilities: On a positive note, the facilities themselves are well-maintained and nice. However, they were incredibly overcrowded during our visit, which detracted from the enjoyment. It was difficult to fully appreciate the amenities when so many people were packed into the space.

Overall Experience: Given the price we paid, the experience was quite average. The combination of parking issues, long wait times, and overcrowding made it hard to recommend Oxygen Jumping for events, especially if you’re looking for a smooth and enjoyable experience.

In summary, while Oxygen Jumping has potential with its facilities, improvements in accessibility, staffing, and crowd management are needed to justify the costs and enhance visitor experience.

Come here for the first time and really want to come back next time. Clean and well maintained playing areas with many helpful staffs to secure the children through their play time. The cafes and toilets are nice. A little bit complex access and parking for car doesn’t reduce kid’s impression for this fun place.
