reviews.text:
I am very disappointed with the service at Cascades Leisure Centre. I spent the entire day trying to call the centre, yet not a single call was answered. This is completely unacceptable for a public-facing business that parents and members rely on.

When I came in to drop my daughter for her swimming lesson, I asked Becky why no one answers the phone. Her response was, “If I’m not busy, I answer. I was busy.” This was shocking to hear — it shows a lack of professionalism and disregard for customers. Answering calls is not optional; it is a basic responsibility of any leisure centre.

The fact that such an important line of communication is being ignored raises serious concerns about how the centre is being managed. It is frustrating, time-wasting, and creates unnecessary stress for parents.

Cascades needs to urgently review its customer service standards and take responsibility for ensuring phones are properly staffed and answered. At present, this level of service is far below what the community deserves.

reviews.text: Canons features an on-site leisure centre, offering a range of activities including swimming, gym facilities, badminton, and gymnastics. The surrounding grounds complement the leisure centre, providing additional amenities such as a well-being centre with a small cafe. Furthermore, the location hosts various events and is enriched by its historical significance.

Dear Canons Leisure management, I am extremely disappointed with the service I received at your leisure centre on Tuesday 26th august , around 4 pm from receptionist lady EUA . The receptionist on duty was not only unhelpful but also rude and dismissive.

When I approached the desk for assistance, she kept her back turned to us and repeatedly said, “everything is online,” without making the slightest effort to help. I explained that I could not access the information online, she simply repeated the same phrase instead of providing any real support.

When I asked for leaflets, she told me there were none available — only for me to later notice a leaflet about swimming lessons on display. This was misleading and left me feeling ignored and dismissed.

Sadly, this is not the first time I’ve experienced this behaviour from the same receptionist, and I know from others that I am not the only one. Her attitude is consistently unprofessional and frankly unacceptable. If all she can do is tell customers to “go online,” then I have to question why she is working at the reception desk at all. This type of behaviour is exactly why your centre is losing customers.

The only positive from this visit was the young man who stepped in after I asked for proper help. He was polite, attentive, and genuinely helpful, showing us around and answering our questions fully. He deserves recognition for doing his job well — something that cannot be said for the receptionist.

I expect this complaint to be taken seriously and for clear action to be taken. Customers deserve to feel welcomed and supported, not dismissed and made to feel like an inconvenience.

Disappointing Experience at Newham Leisure Centre Football Pitch

We play football at Newham Leisure Centre every Wednesday and have been doing so regularly. Unfortunately, the experience has been consistently frustrating. The pitch is in poor condition – it’s mostly dirt, and the net is either missing or completely ripped. Despite this, we continue to book it (paying £77) simply because of its convenient location.

We normally book the pitch from 10am to 11am, but unfortunately, today we selected the wrong time and booked it for 11am to 12pm by mistake. Since all the players had arrived early and the pitch is always empty except for us, we politely requested for it to be opened at 10am. Ed, the staff member on duty, eventually opened the pitch at 10:50am, and then kicked us off at 11:30am – insisting that our time had started when he unlocked it. That left us with only 30 minutes of playtime, despite having paid for a full hour.

When I went to reception to speak to a manager (as Ed advised), it turned out he was the manager – making it very uncomfortable to raise our concerns. I explained that this isn’t a one-off issue: the pitch is rarely open on time, and we regularly have to ask staff to unlock it, which cuts into our paid time. Unfortunately, Ed was extremely unprofessional and dismissive during the conversation.

We are very disappointed with the way the facility is managed and the lack of customer care, especially for regulars. Hopefully, the centre takes feedback seriously and makes the necessary improvements.

reviews.text:
We visited Oxygen Romford as a family of five — two adults and three children aged 17, 15, and 7 — hoping to spend some fun, active time together. Our goal was to enjoy it as a full-family activity, but the reality turned out to be different.
Unfortunately, it quickly became clear that the park is not designed for older kids or adults. The teens were bored almost immediately — there was nothing engaging for their age group — and as adults, we didn’t feel comfortable jumping in the same space as small children. It felt unsafe and awkward, with a real risk of accidentally bumping into or injuring a younger child. In the end, four out of five tickets were basically wasted.
That said, the experience was great for our 7-year-old — he had a fantastic time! The layout and activities are clearly aimed at kids under 10, and for that age group, it’s very enjoyable. Also, a big plus is the café area for parents. It offers a clear view of the entire trampoline zone, which means you can sit down, relax, and still keep an eye on your child at all times. That visibility is a huge advantage for parents.

Our suggestion: The website should clearly state the recommended maximum age for participants. It would help families avoid disappointment and ensure a safer environment for the younger children.

We might return — but only with our youngest next time.
Staff are lovely. Took my nephew here for the first time. He loved it. Reception team were friendly and helpful. Play area was massive. Seating area was clean and thr coffee was good.

I just had a great time at this venue! The team were absolutely brilliant – really welcoming and friendly throughout my visit, which made all the difference. Everything was spotless and the value for money was spot on. The only hiccup was the temperature; it was a bit too warm for comfort. Overall, I can't wait to go back!

I took my three kids to this venue, and they had an absolute blast! My youngest, who has severe autism, really loved the soft play and trampolines. The place was air-conditioned and not too busy, which made it even better. The staff were super friendly and always around if we needed help. Plus, I couldn't get enough of their fresh blueberry muffin—just delicious! Definitely a fantastic place for a family outing!

We came to celebrate my son’s birthday with his friends, but he was refused access to the trampoline because of his disability (Down syndrome). I was told that this counted as a “physical disability” and that he could not participate without a doctor’s note. This decision left my son heartbroken, in tears, and excluded from on his  birthday celebration.

Not only was this discriminatory, but it was also handled without compassion. Families like mine should be able to access activities in an inclusive environment without facing barriers that single out children with disabilities. The Equality Act 2010 (if you are in the UK) requires businesses to make reasonable adjustments so that disabled people are not treated unfavourably compared to others. Refusing my son access in this way is both unfair and discriminatory.

I am requesting the following:
1.	A full written apology for the distress caused to my son and family.
2.	An immediate review of your policies to ensure children with disabilities are treated fairly and inclusively in line with equality legislation.
3.	Staff training on disability awareness and inclusion so that no other child has to experience what my son went through today.

I expect a prompt response to this matter. Please be aware that if I do not receive a satisfactory reply, I will escalate this complaint to the relevant authorities and will also consider sharing this experience publicly. I will take this up and make sure action is taken—I will not let this matter slide.

Filthiest gym ever. I have been a paying member for two years when I lived in Peckham and used East Dulwich and Peckham leisure centres which were clean. Use to come here as a kid and needed a redurb then. Took my kids and was genuinely shocked that they are allowed to be open! Green everywhere, bodyfat and grit maybe even sand in the actual pool.
I use to be a life guard, i know its incredibly boring, but lord almighty they all seem like they were on death row.

Couldn't possibly recommend. Some pictures below but they do not do the mess justice.

Horrible gym, if we can actually call it that. Lacking in machines, equipment and facilities to do anything. And to have the cherry on top staff is not helpful at all, they are just sitting playing games in their phones

So unsatisfied in general, not recommended to anyone.

I never write negative reviews (no, honestly!) but I absolutely have to in this instance.
I've just been to a morning swim (7.30am) and the state of the showers were absolutely shocking. SHOCKING.

There were bunches of hair everywhere. I'm not talking a bit of hair but bunches and bunches all over the wall, the drains, the door, everywhere. The shower when I entered was bone dry, which means it's not been used yet ahead of me, which would also mean that the showers were not cleaned with closing last night or upon opening today.
To add to this, the shower are is full of these small, black flies, there must have been at least 50 inside the shower cubicle and they landed on me as I showered. It was horrendous. I've given up literally mid shower and dried up and left.

I'm unsure how Southwark Council can justify updating and refreshing the equipment of their Leisure Centres at the moment when clearly, they are lightyears away from getting the basics covered, such as a minimum standard of hygiene.

reviews.text:
The sports hall at Academy Sports Centre has been dangerously slippery for weeks, leading to multiple falls and serious injuries. In our last session alone, three players slipped, with one suffering a debilitating knee injury. Despite ongoing concerns, the issue remains unresolved.

The problem seems to stem from ineffective cleaning—court sweepers are used, but they do not remove the dust that makes the floor dangerously slick. Proper mopping with water is essential to ensure a safe playing surface.

In addition, some of the reception staff have been extremely unwelcoming and impolite. Their attitude feels dismissive, and at times, it raises concerns about whether there are underlying biases at play. This kind of behaviour does not reflect well on the centre and makes the overall experience even more frustrating.

reviews.text: Absolutely love this model village. We went here on the drive home to pop in as we went when we were kids (now 30) and we enjoyed it just as much. We love the place, it brings so much tranquility and soothe as it moves you in time and place of calm, order and simpler life. The scenery and each detail make you appreciate the way of life we have lost, seems so precious.
Pay attention to details - like name on the shops and venues, make you giggle, the train stations and trains running everywhere (the bridge by the castle!). And the horticultural care - what a masterpiece of mini elms, pines, little rivers, cascades. There is a short train ride for families and you can have some fun with operating a boat on a pond. Plenty of koi carps, would be great if we could feed them, too! (Please sell the fish food with tickets!) We discovered new room where old type writer is, what a great fun to do some scenarios and play with props. Playground is also awesome for kids, good food selection in cafe (although I would like to see more healthier options) and plenty of seating area (you can bring your own food). Thank you for being there :)

reviews.text:
We had the most amazing time at Go Ape and I can’t recommend it highly enough! From the moment we arrived, the whole experience was smooth, professional, and fun. The staff greeted us warmly and were super helpful throughout the entire visit. They took safety seriously, walking us through every detail in a clear and friendly way which definitely helped settle a few nerves in the group.

Once we got into the trees, the real adventure began. The course was fantastic a great mix of rope bridges, wobbly crossings, climbing elements, and of course the zip lines, which were the absolute highlight for everyone. Each section brought a new challenge and new laughs. It felt empowering to push through the tougher parts, especially knowing the harnesses and safety systems were rock-solid.

The scenery was beautiful too. Being up in the trees, completely surrounded by nature, made it feel like a mini escape from everyday life. It was peaceful and exhilarating all at once. You could feel the breeze up high, and then suddenly you’re flying down a zip line with the biggest smile on your face.

What really stood out was how well-run everything was. The team was always nearby in case you needed help, but they also gave you the freedom to go at your own pace. Whether you’re a thrill seeker or someone just trying to get out of your comfort zone, Go Ape strikes the perfect balance of excitement and safety. It’s also a fantastic workout without even realizing it!

I went with my partner, but it is also a great outing for families and friends, or even solo as you’ll be in a group with random people who you could make friends with. I know we definitely did. Everyone came away talking about how much fun they had.

reviews.text: Always have the best time learning at Gillian’s! All the instructors are professional and very hands on , especially Kieran, and they have several lovely horses that are well taken care of! There are lots of children learning as well, and I can tell that they all enjoy their time at the stables. If it is not too far from where I live in London, I would definitely go every week. But to say that I travel 2 hours one way just to get a session on Saturday means that I really enjoy my time at Gillian’s.

I have ridden at Gillian's 2-3 times a week for the last year and I can highly recommend the riding school. They have a large range of horses and ponies to suit all rider capabilities, including complete beginners. They have an active pony club and are very busy on school holidays when they offer activity days. The demand for lessons is quite high so you do need to book in advance. I can also highly recommend for anyone wanting to start riding for BSR Horse Riding Test, as they excel at training complete beginners.

The stable blocks are stables are quite large, the horses and ponies are well looked after. The staff were working around the clock over the Christmas break boiling kettles every hour to ensure the automatic water feeders didn't freeze when it was below zero. The farrier is out regularly.

They offer 1hr woodland rides, rides to the gallops (2hrs) to Trent Park, group lessons, private lessons and an opportunity to go to shows. They have a large indoor arena and a smaller outdoor one. The cross country lessons in summer are the most fun. All the instructors are great. There's also a stable goat around 7 stable peacocks which are free-roaming and quite impressive. Couldn't recommend highly enough.

I’ve been at Gillian’s for 20 years now, first as a client, then staff and now solely as a livery.

Growing up, the brilliant horses and instructors at Gillian’s sparked my passion and are the reason I became obsessed. I’ve learned everything I know about horses and riding here and can’t recommend it enough as a down to earth, family run yard.

I’ve kept my horse here for 10 years and Gill and Danny have always been accommodating and on hand to give advice. They were both fantastic when my horse has had to have surgeries and made transporting and rehabbing her as stress free as possible. The yard has a good routine, knowledgable staff and high standards. I wouldn’t feel happy stabling my horse anywhere else.

His knowledge, patience, and encouragement have made such a difference to my confidence, and every lesson is something I genuinely look forward to.

The horses are so well cared for — it’s clear how much love and attention they receive from everyone at the yard. All the staff are incredibly kind, welcoming, and always happy to help, whether you’re a total beginner or a more experienced rider.

It’s such a positive and welcoming place. If you’re thinking about starting riding or looking to get back into it, this is definitely the place to go!

reviews.text:
Amazing place for a day out and watch some miniature railway stock in action .
Day out was superb.
Really fun day. The miniature railway was a decent length and my two boys loved it. The grounds are also very cool - quirky design with sculptures dotted around. We liked it lots. Strong recommend.

We visited on one of the miniature railway open days. Unfortunately we got there quite late on the Saturday afternoon due to our sons nap so we only managed to go on the steam engine which was approx a 30 mom journey. There were two other trains operating that day and we'll definitely be back to go on the diesel and electric trains. The queue to pay for tickets is really slow. It's also confusing as it merges with the cafe queue. It's slowed down further by the members of staff explaining the same information to each customer. A board with info as you enter would save lots of time. There is a little station platform although there is little queue management. We were the second customers prior to one train but as the staff didn't know which platform the next train would go from, we stood on the wrong one and by the time the train came in and we swapped platforms, the train had filled up and we had to wait for the next one. Not ideal with an 18 month old. A little more organisation would go a long way. The trains go quite far through nice woodland and gardens. We'd like to have explore the gardens but they were closed on the day we visited. Overall, a great day out for young families and we'll definitely be returning. Good value for money too.
We had a wonderful few hours walking round the sculptures & a wonderful train ride.  All the staff were so helpful & friendly would thoroughly recommend

We had this Miniature railway on the list for a visit for a long time, and with a day with nothing planned we spotted it was open and took the trip over to see what it was like.

The railway is situated in the grounds of Barnards and as you enter through the gate you turn left and park next to the miniature railway station / hub. The station area had picnic benches, a small cafe (think crisps and cake with drinks but not much more than that), and toilets.

Tickets for the railway is £7 per person, no difference between kids and adults prices, and all day ticket is £10, so if doing more than one trip that's the way to go. We were given option of buying the single and then just upgrading for the difference, which I guess is a good idea if you think its going to rain and / or not sure if your kids will like it.

They have a variety of trains, on our visit it was a steam, diesel and an electric train. The diesel does the whole route and back, the steam goes to the station before the end (issues with going up slight incline) and the electric was doing a slightly different route to the lake.

You can get off at the stations and have a wonder around, but we visited when the gardens were not open and thus we was a little more limited on where we were allowed to walk. On days where the gardens are shut, you are limited to the left of the river and can not cross the runway area (see map!). The gardens looked good with some interesting statues.

The only thing I was a little unsure about is what happens when it's busy? The trains only have limited capacity and as mentioned above if you get off then you are hoping there is space on another train....! Trains run every 20 mins ish, so not a massive wait, but I did wonder...! Thankfully no issues with space for us.

Staff were all friendly and we had a really nice visit. Would certainly visit again.

reviews.text: The museum itself is free! Though there is a cost for parking, plenty of room when I went. There are 6 hangars with aircraft from the dawn of aviation through to a mockup of an F35. There are information boards about each aircraft plus other static displays. There is a childrens play area outside and a cafe, plus of course a shop. Some air museums have rope barriers that are well away from the aircraft, but not here, you can get as close as safety and conservation allow, so lots of closeup photo opportunities. Some aircraft have steps next to them, plus some hangars have raised viewing areas. You can walk through a Sunderland flying boat. I did the Cold War experience, this is a charged extra - book well in advance. I sat in the Vulcan and Phantom and got inside the ropes with the Lightning, Vampire and several other aircraft on a one-to-one tour that was excellent, the guide was great. The tour was about 90 mins and proceeded at a good pace, it didn't feel rushed. In total I was in the museum for 4.5hrs, didn't stop for lunch, and took a large number of photos. Great day!

Oh. wow, you could spend literally days here and not see everything. You do need to get tickets prior to coming but to be honest, I didn't know that so I did it on line and it came through almost immediately and so it didn't impinge on me getting in at all. Certainly if your interested and like to read the entries. I am interested and I spent four hours, which was only scratching the surface. I had tea and cake which was excellent and did something I very rarely do, I bought some items from the shop, a Red Arrows cap for my grandson and an RAF tee-shirt, indulging myself. Considering this exhibition is free I can honestly say it is exceptional value for anyone, including families. The parking is fairly expensive by Yorkshire standards, but probably not by London. As you can read I was bowled over by the amount of exhibits which are grouped into buildings which form a historical timeline from the pre-inception days when it was a gentleman's hobby, into the first world war and the meteoric rise in the speed, manoeuvrability and firepower. Then on to the second world war, Spitfire, Hurricane, Lancaster and Halifax, to name but a few of the famous names. Then on through the Jet age into the present day, with the RAF's latest fighter/Bombers and missiles. Awesome, absolutely awesome and I will most definitely  be back to finish my tour and maybe just go round again because I will most certainly have missed loads.

What a lovely museum! The stories are incredible and they have a large variety of aircraft from different countries. I could also really appreciate the engines that are shown next to most of the aircraft.

I would recommend it to anyone who loves planes, engine and war history.

I visited the Royal Air Force Museum London today and had a fantastic experience. The collection of aircraft is impressive and well presented — from iconic WWII planes to modern jets. The exhibitions are informative, interactive, and suitable for all ages. The museum does a great job of combining history with personal stories, making it engaging rather than just technical.

It’s free to enter (donations welcome), and the staff are very friendly and knowledgeable. The layout is spacious, with plenty of room to explore at your own pace. There are also cafés and a gift shop on-site.

Highly recommend this museum for anyone interested in aviation, history, or just looking for a great day out in London.

So much to see. So many restorations and truly impressive pieces of history. I spent a brisk 3 hours here and could’ve spent another 3 reading all the accounts, historical documents and displays. You’ll get your steps in walking between each of the hangers. A couple food options mean taking a break a grabbing a bite is a good option. This museum is a must for any aviation enthusiast.

This place is inclusive and the calming atmosphere of the centre resonates with it’s commitment to making the equestrian experience accessible to everyone.

The worst pony centre ever, there was a lady who explains to children how to do gymnastics on the horse back she was very tough and rude with all children, mine and my friends children no longer want to go again.

Difficult to contact with. I have been asking for riding lessons and barely after months i got my answer. It felt like i was chasing them.

Unfortunately the coach there Ailbhe was not welcoming at all. I gave up on the stable.

Other than that it seems like a nice stable and the volunteers were nice ..

result.formatted_address: Parkfields Rd, Kingston upon Thames KT2 5LL, UK

reviews.text: I have been struggling to find a good riding school that allows me to wear the safety gear I wanted. I almost gave up until I found Barnfield! Not only were they happy with it they encouraged saftey too! Another thing that blew me away about this riding school is that they really care about their clients enjoying their riding experience and I really appreciated this. Encouragement and a positive nature as well as constructive feedback is what makes a quality instructor and I felt this while riding at Barnfield. I'm always keen to learn from stables about the horse experience and Barnfield is one of the few places I went to that seemed invested in this so it is one of the things that will keep me coming back. The last thing I want to say is that they were very welcoming to me and treated me like a person, and I know this seems a very basic thing to say but good customer service goes a long way! Some places I've been to treated me like I wasn't worth the time of day because they are too busy. Barnfield is a busy school, but they still take time to smile and welcome you and let you know where you stand and where you need to go next/ what you need to do, and that is really important. Thank you everyone at Barnfield Riding school! Xxx

I have been to Barnfield riding school with my partner every week for the past two years. We have always had a great time and we want to thank Patsy and her staff for always being helpful and patient with us, not least special thanks to the horses and ponies that we ride including Ameera, Candy, Mr. T, Tessie, Jazz, Sienna, Star and others!

I have been riding at Barnfield for some time. It is a very professional, welcoming Riding School where the horses & ponies receive consistent, high quality care plus a lot of love! There are enough different instructors so you can find the one that suits you, or chop & change as you wish. A holistic approach to riding is offered with a mixture of lessons in the arena, on the mechanical horse & out hacking. All clients are encouraged to interact with the horses to widen their knowledge. I recommend Barnfield to anyone who loves horses, & wants a hands-on approach to learning to ride.

I have been riding at Barnfield for many years and would highly recommend this wonderful riding school. The standard of teaching is high, and the instructors are dedicated to both the welfare of the client, and the individual horses, and everyone’s enjoyment all round.
The staff are friendly, the horses are loved and are well cared for, with their individual needs being met. Barnfield has the welcoming atmosphere and hands-on personable approach that many of the larger riding schools nowadays lack.  Of course I keep coming back because I’ve still got so much more to learn, I love the friendly inclusive atmosphere, and my favourite wonderful horses!

I am a new retiree and have recently become a volunteer at Barnfield Riding for Disabled/Riding School.

I didn’t know what to expect …but the kindness and expert care shown to the horses and clients is exactly what I hoped.
At age 66..and having not ridden for many many  years..I have been inspired by the staff here to soon start my own riding lessons and aim to get back in the saddle…something I never thought I would ever do.

I unreservedly recommend.  (maybe anyone reading this might consider volunteering too?)

reviews.text: I booked a "have a go” session .The staff were welcoming and supportive, the horses were well cared for, and the venue was very clean and well maintained. The experience has given me confidence and I’m now considering taking lessons here. I would definitely recommend this place to friends and family. But it would be nice to have a small café or more drink and food options available. Things like protein bars, snacks, or light refreshments before or after the sessions would make the visit even better.

I’ve been taking private lessons with Kerrie at Lee Valley for a couple of years now. I absolutely love coming here, it’s a highlight of my week. I find the reception staff friendly and helpful, the horses and ponies are so well cared for and seem very happy. Kerrie’s a wonderful instructor, she made me feel comfortable as an adult new rider when I initially started taking lessons. I have fun, learn and gain confidence in each lesson.

Today I had a lesson with Andrea, an excellent instructor! His is not only a skillful rider, a nice and gentle person but also a great instructor!  He is good at giving the instructions with explanation of the reasons why I should do so, and tell me to feel the connection with the horse . the experience was comfortable and the nice! I found myself can get the key points easily! Thanks to him! I wish the Riding centre could have a consideration of a promotion or a stuff award for him!

Amazing experience, my 14 year old child loved it a lot. The instructor was good and clear with her instructions, not sure what her name was. The receptionist, Maggie, was super helpful and welcoming. She helped us a lot and got us settled, also helped us with a mistake we did with the booking. It was a really amazing experience., we'll see you soon.

I cannot praise this school enough. A very welcoming environment and the level of knowledge is second to none. The front of house team have always been so lovely to me, and to anyone I bring with me to my lessons, and very approcable. They always call me back when I send 20 emails (sorry haha) My favourite instructor is Severia, she is so knowledgeable, approachable and an all around lovely person. She pushes to get the best out of you in every lesson. I cannot wait for my niece to start learning with her. She has genuinely given me so much confidence and encouragement. This school should be proud to have such an outstanding instructor. She is a credit to this company.

The people here are all wonderful, Billie and Farrah are also so brilliant, and Vicki is an absolute diamond. I feel so comfortable here.

Great school!

Very cute farm with horse rides my kids enjoyed it. ( horse rides need advanced booking ) Also the walk to the farm is very beautiful. People who love nature walks I total recommend this place.

The staff in the cafe could have been more friendly but other wise all good xx

Nice farm, the access is free but they really appreciate donations for helping the farm and the animals! There’s a nice little play area with wooden playground activities for kids, and close to that some picnic tables, and a nice cafe with indoor seats too. You can also buy food for feeding sheep and goats, there are several animals and there’s a chance to prebook activities to do with some of the animals (including riding horses/pony!)
It’s a nice place to go to, even for a couple of hours :)
Don’t forget your wellies if there’s been a rainy weather before, it can be quite muddy (but still fun!)

Awesome place to visit with young children and adults alike. Cute little animals. Café is okay too, a little souvenir shop if you want to buy anything, free entry but please do not forget a small donation of at least £2 as it helps the farm with the up keep of its animals. Free parking, but spaces are limited. Narrow rough road towards parking, so drive extra carefully please.

Went to feed the animals whilst walking past on the way to Abbey Mills. We were less than half hour in there but it is a cute place with a cafe. A donation is required upon arrival but they take card and cash.

Decided to drop in as I was staying a short distance from the Farm, and saw that they had ferrets. Was not disappointed at all! The variety of animals cared for was quite interesting, some of which I've not seen before.

The staff were lovely, the animals seem very well looked after indeed and all around it's a nice place to spend a couple of hours 😁

Well worth a visit if you're in the Merton area.

reviews.text: Took the kids and 1 adult to the equestrian centre today. Easy system - line up at the office, pay, change into the available boots/wellies as required, then line up to get your helmet. Reasonably priced. Each rider did 4 laps for £5. You need to supervise your younger kids riding. Wear long bottoms - no shorts / skirts / dresses. Vending machine near office. Friendly staff. Plenty of car park space.

I honestly wish i could rate it 0 stars! This place is honestly inappropriate the way the staff treat people of colour and those of a bigger size is actually horrible. My niece was so excited to come for horse riding as it was her dream as a child. It was a way for her to get away from everything, but this place brought nothing but trouble for the family. Not only was she called derogatory racial slurs but she and her friends were made fun of BY THE STAFF for not being the smallest of sizes! Can you imagine that? Your daughter being made to feel dehumanised! I was honestly distraught when my niece told me this. Please do better and TAKE YOUR CHILD ANY WHERE BUT HERE FOR THEIR SAKE AND YOURS.

What happened to the welcoming society we used to know and love?

I took lessons here for four months and the experience was disappointing.

1️⃣Cancellation system is confusing and unfair even after notifying them in advance, I was told I “missed” classes and lost my deposit twice.
2️⃣Poor communication with coach.
3️⃣Very slow progress after months of lessons I felt little improvement after first 2 lessons.
4️⃣Uncomfortable atmosphere one staff member was intimidating, which made the lessons stressful rather than enjoyable.

I have decided to leave, and I won’t recommend it unless you are extremely close to it.

My sons, loved it. Staff were friendly and helpful. Horses were looked after and well kempt.
We went for their drop in horse and pony ride session. 5 laps at £5 which i thought was pretty decent. They do have a riding school avaible too.
Lovely for children. They have free loan wellies for those who don't have or forget. Just make sure you wear full length trousers.
They do require you to wear a mask, so bring one along or pay £1 per mask. For anyone riding and for those guiding a young child.

I rode here for almost 5 months. I enjoyed my lessons with Dawn but overall progress is extremely slow. Despite making good progress I was kept on a lead rein for 5 months and most of my lessons consisted of walking with a side of trot holding on to the saddle. As soon as I changed schools, I progressed much faster and was immediately let off the lead and learned to trot independently and canter. My new trainer was shocked at how little I’d learned. I also feel as though the booking system is quite inflexible which is the main reason I stopped riding here.

reviews.text:
Really lovely staff very helpful, great riding school offering 1hr lessons for £40 (£65 if riding in the forest). The horses are well kept and looked after & they are just beautiful animals.  The also offer pony rides during summer holidays.
You can also park you car via empress avenue, which also gives you access to the forest and ponds.

I've been taking my 11yr old son- (who has additional needs)to Aldersbrook Horses and Ponies for about 10 weeks. We go to the Sat/Sun drop in session and we have been so impressed.  The staff are so friendly, patient and knowledgeable about how to manage their animals and the children riding them. My son has made week on week progress which has increased his confidence and self esteem. He has been treated so calmly and kindly by staff, he hasn't had an extra curricular activity up until now that he hasn't needed persuading to go to.  We won't be stopping any time soon...I just hope he doesn't ask for his own pony for his next birthday 😂😂 thank you to all of you at Aldersbrook Horses and Ponies - you have been so patient, friendly and kind, it has enriched my son's life without a doubt

My daughter spends most of her free time at Aldersbrook Horses and Ponies and in that time, Julie and Cheyenne have been amazing at teaching her how to care for and ride the Ponies that she has a share in. There are a lovely group of volunteers and it has such a welcome community feel. I’d highly recommend them if you are new to riding or have some experience as they can support people of all ages and experience. The horses and ponies are well cared for and loved.

The horses are always well looked after. Although the yard ain't always as clean as some stables it's not an issue. The staff are always very friendly and it's a great place to do work experience. I've added some photos of when I did my work experience

all the horses are so sweet, good instructors
sunday drop in lessons for first time
: £15 9:30, 10:00 and 10:30 am

reviews.text:
I can’t recommend Chigwell Riding Trust enough, especially the incredible Deborah. She’s not only a fantastic teacher - patient, knowledgeable, and encouraging - but also one of the kindest people you could meet. She has a way of making everyone feel comfortable and confident, whether it’s your first time riding or you’ve been coming for years!

I also had the chance to volunteer and was made to feel so welcome from the very start. It opened my eyes to just how vital the Trust is for children with special needs. The horses truly aid their development, confidence, and joy in such a powerful way. The atmosphere is uplifting, and Deborah’s dedication makes the experience even more meaningful.
VERY well looked after horses, very friendly staff, and an immensely worthy trust!

Excellent for children with special needs and adults with disabilities. Ample parking, good rates and exceptionally friendly and helpful staff helps to tick all the boxes. Only downside is the waiting list which can take up to three years due to demand. This is a voluntary organisation so you need to contribute by paying on time and chipping in to help other users. You will not be disappointed.

I have been riding here for over 40 years.  Great place and very friendly.  Only thing I would do is build another place like it somewhere in the Essex Area, not as a rival, but to work alongside Chigwell to take some of the waiting list on and cut waiting times for all concerned.  New riders would either go to Chigwell or the other place wherever it was

Chiggers has been my horsey home for 24 years. The horse's have given me a body I can use independently. The volunteers are humble, staff committed and animals magical.
It is impossible to explain how much joy, confidence, faith and mobility 45 minutes on a horse who is your friend can give you. Thank you all

result.name: The Horse Rangers Association (Hampton Court)

reviews.text:
I joined in 1967 or 1968, when I was 12 or 13. It was an incredible experience. I'd barely touched a horse as we could never afford contact with them, but I was totally horse mad. I loved every aspect of my Saturdays -- riding, of course, but also mucking out, grooming, cleaning tack. The first aid lessons were helpful. And we all survived the square bashing. Such fond memories!
I realise this review might not be too relevant. But I wish today's HRA well.

I think the HRA is a fantastic organisation in principle however as a child 20 to 25 years ago it severely damaged my mental health and my mental health has suffered since. It was rife with bullying, girls in cliques as senior officers, no meritocracy and no policies or procedures to enforce any proper rules and boundaries. It left me with a love of horses but also a profound sadness, not caused by the horses but the terrible regime of young women bullying girls, not rewarding merit just punishing those already down and in my case a little overweight and lacking confidence at the time. I then developed anorexia aged 15 from which I’ve still not recovered from 23 years later. I hope this has been fixed as I’m not the only one, it damaged many and that impact proportionately may be greater than those who it helped.

Very disappointing. During a 4.5hr session, my 10 year old daughter has regularly been left in a hut and allowed to clock up 3+ hours of screentime on a mobile phone. This constitutes neglect and inadequate supervision. The contact with the horses might be good, but there is a lot of unstructured sitting around and the sessions are poorly organised.
Amazing center that truly cares for their kids and horses. Would definitely recommend !
Amazing charity please donate £10 to them to keep them open for long features

reviews.text:
We visit the charity as part of organised support by The Worshipful Company of Horn and Plastics. We were greeted by happy, welcoming and caring staff and volunteers. Some of them shared their stories and experiences and how working or interacting with horses have helped them to get through hard times and be in a happy place. Here is their websites message to prople.

“Horses, kindness, a place to be yourself.

We’re an award winning charity and Riding for the Disabled Association centre. We strive to be a place where horses help people and people help horses, always leaving happier than when they arrived.”

They are continually looking for donations, support and visitors.

Park Lane is a wonderful place!  Everyone is so welcoming and kind and whatever your ability or experience, you are made to feel valued.  We have seen first hand the difference it has made and we are so grateful that we have found this very special place!  It's not just about the riding - it's about learning about how to care for the horses, working together, being part of a team and finding where you can thrive. They really take the time to get to know and care about each individual and what they can do.  Thank you to EVERYONE involved!

I’ve been volunteering at Park Lane Stables for around 8 months now. It’s one of the best things I’ve ever done! Lovely people, wonderful horses and great to spend time in nature doing something meaningful for the community.

I rang Park Lane Stables and within in 2 weeks at the age of 61 i was riding my first ever horse. The horses are very well kept and all the staff and volunteers are lovely. Jo and lexi my trainers are fantastic, encouraging and understanding. The owner Natalie is a superstar. I have now had 3 rides with them since february and already riding without assistance and looking forward to entering competions. I am very disabled but no one would know this if i did not say.
Thank you Park lane stables

Park Lane stables is a very special place. Having ridden for over 40 years and had my own horses growing up, I have experienced a number of stables and none compare to the warmth and generosity of spirit at Park Lane. Kindness and inclusivity are at the heart of everything they do, with horse and human welfare at the forefront and activities to suit all ages and abilities. The team of staff and volunteers are a joy, always smiling, always welcoming with a wealth of knowledge and experience. As for the horses - they are a delight (!) and riding them in Bushy Park always feels like a treat. Myself and my young nieces love being a part of the Park Lane family. As a Teddington resident I am also lucky to live close by and their return to the town has been nothing short of wonderful for the community and for clients like me. Regardless of where you live, Park Lane really is a place where you feel at home.
Jo Johnson, Teddington

reviews.text: Had my first half hour lesson here with Natalie and Charlie today - really enjoyed it! Natalie built on my previous experience and was really patient. Charlie was also a lovely horse to ride, calm and patient :) I’ll definitely be back, thank you so much!

After a lot of research on different stables I decided to go for Ruislip Park Stables and I’m so glad I did.
I booked the 45 minute woodland lesson for two, as a birthday treat for a friend and we had the most amazing experience. We had Natalie as our instructor and she was so lovely and made the experience so enjoyable. We were riding by ourselves and trotting with guidance by the end of our lesson. Highly recommend and will be returning very soon.
Took my 3 year old for his first pony ride and it was great . He loved it walking around the woods on the pony and all the girls were super friendly and nice.

A couple of months ago, we used your services; just like we’ve done many times before.

My daughter, after visiting over 10 times, had one simple wish: to ride the black and white horse. When I made the booking, I was told it wasn’t guaranteed, which I completely understood. However, when we arrived and I asked again, the response I got (accompanied by an impressively disgusted facial expression) was a firm no, followed by, “We don’t take bookings for specific horses.” Fair enough.

What’s harder to understand is the level of disdain and rudeness with which we were treated. From a tall blonde woman working with the horses, to the owner and the manager. None of them could have been less professional.

At one point, the manager even shouted to the owner in front of several customers that she shouldn’t  speak to me anymore because, in his words, “she is not coming back anyway.” Well, he was certainly right about that!

Never in any place have we felt so unwelcome or treated with such contempt.

I could go into more detail, but I’ll spare everyone the novel-length version of this experience.

Thanks for absolutely nothing. Best of luck—you’re going to need it.

My daughter had another amazing party experience.  Everyone was friendly.
Mum’s that came commented on how , talkative and caring the staff were.

reviews.text:
We had a great time here at the summer beach ‘Norden-by-the-Sea’ they do for children/families.
Took our 3.7 year old granddaughter who absolutely loved playing in the sand and boat. We stayed about 3 hours and had coffees, lunch and a drink. Good range of food choices for big and little people. Good service. Toilets a little on the messy side but not too bad considering how busy it was.
My first visit here to attend a live Show. I had a beer, fish and chips outdoors at the cafe. The Theatre was lovely, except being in the front row, the stage was too high. A nice experience though

A really fantastic venue on the outskirts of Maidenhead.  I only had time to attend a gig in the studio which was converted for the evening into an intimate theatre.  Very friendly staff and very well curated.
We got a free kite making workshop as my daughter is a young carer. Kids loved it. Food is good but couple of items on the menu weren't available

Visited to watch a film that wasn’t on in the mainstream cinemas; easy to book and cheaper. Coffee shop/bar had a good selection of drinks and snacks.

Loads of parking and all in all a pleasant visit.

As well as visiting for the film we also went along to the Craft Market they had on Saturday night. No parking on site but they’d sorted parking out a tire school up the inroad. A good variety of stalls, including hot food, there was live music and a bar, we had a lovely time.

result.formatted_address: 130 Herne Hill, London SE24 9QL, UK
result.name: South London Dance School

reviews.text:
My daughter attended South London Dance Studio for 10 years, and the classes made her what she is today. From her very first class, she was welcomed into a nurturing and professional environment that taught her how to dance and so much more.

Over the years, she trained in multiple dance genres including ballet, modern, tap, and street. The strength, flexibility, and focus she developed translated beautifully into other activities like gymnastics and swimming. The exacting standards showed her what was possible when you apply yourself. The quality of teaching is exceptional. All the teachers we met were passionate, highly skilled, and genuinely invested in each student's progress and well-being.

The studio’s shows are spectacular. From the choreography to the costumes, staging, and overall delivery, the performances are of a professional standard and a real highlight for both dancers and families. Watching my daughter perform in these productions was a joy and a testament to the studio’s commitment to excellence.

I wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone looking for top-tier dance training in a supportive, inspiring and inclusive environment.

Before enrolling my 5-year-old daughter, I checked the reviews and noticed quite a few negative comments about the school’s aggressive approach to cancellations and communication. However, I had also heard good things about their teaching staff, so I decided to give it a try and registered my daughter for Saturday lessons. She did enjoy the classes, and I do appreciate the quality of their teaching.

That said, their communication style left a lot to be desired. Emails were overly long, with important information buried in lengthy paragraphs, which I found quite frustrating. At the beginning of the term, I decided to give a polite notification about leaving, citing a busy schedule and the possibility of trying weekday lessons instead. Natasha responded very quickly and, without asking, enrolled my daughter in Monday lessons. I explained that we couldn’t do Mondays, and she immediately asked if she could register her for Wednesday instead. I didn’t reply to this email, meaning I didn’t confirm anything.

To my surprise, after half-term, I received an email stating that my daughter had been registered for Wednesday lessons—even though I never confirmed this. They are now pushing me to pay the invoice for a term we never agreed to, which has left me shocked by how aggressive their approach is. This kind of attitude doesn’t feel appropriate for a dance school, and it’s not something I can trust.

While the teaching quality may be good, the administrative side of things needs a lot of improvement. I can’t recommend the school due to this unpleasant experience.

My daughter attends this school and she always comes home from lessons feeling inspired to dance even more and work on the corrections she was given. She is always excited to go to lessons and expresses to me how she loves all of her classmates, teachers and dance. She describes her teachers as strict in the best way possible and appreciates them greatly. They are all very very friendly!

I don't normally write bad reviews but this time I really need to. I had adult tap lessons for 6 months but before the third term they decided they were changing the timetable. I said I wasn't sure I could continue and a week after the close off date I confirmed that and they told me I still had to pay the full fees and added lots of charges for the lateness as I protested that I had never confirmed that I could. This was before the summer holidays so lots of time in reality before the lessons in September (3 months!) I am sorry to have to leave the school but I am very happy that I have found a more professional environment with much more reasonable prices and terms and conditions and someone who has a much nicer email tone than this school.

I rarely write negative reviews, but this time I must! I attended adult ballet classes for over two years, always paying my fees promptly upon receiving the invoice. Unfortunately, a sudden change at my workplace prevented me from attending the next term (January/April). I informed them, albeit slightly late within the notice period, apologising and explaining the circumstances. Despite still being two weeks away from receiving the invoice for the next term, the back office showed no mercy. They aggressively demanded payment for the entire term I could no longer attend.

I'd paid half of the fee as a gesture of goodwill, but they insisted on the full amount, citing their rigid Terms & Conditions. All they wanted was to be paid and couldn't care any less. It's ironic for a dance school to show zero flexibility with its clients. Eventually, I had no choice but to pay for the entire term. It's a shame because I had enjoyed the classes with nice teachers for more than two years, but the back office ruined the whole experience by making it very stressful. My sister was also upset by their inflexibility and decided to stop attending classes there after 4 years. By doing so you've lost another client, well done! I'm relieved to have found a better and more professional ballet school now!

reviews.text: Absolutely magical. I can’t recommend this enough. Beautiful building, wonderful fun and great value.
Such a wonderful experience for young children! So well organised, so interactive and child centred. Always such a pleasure to bring my grandchildren.

As a beginner, I found Saraswati yoga to be a friendly and inclusive environment, offering a perfect blend of yoga with some meditation. After a few months of attending I no longer have lower back pain when riding to work, and I sleep better at night.

Namaste

Compassionate, knowledgeable, friendly teachers in a calming setting.
Beginner to advanced you’re welcome here.

You can attend a variety of classes without needing to book in advance.  Saraswati  also puts on day workshops and mindfulness courses of which I have attended.  She shares updates on research.  All the instructors are very approachable and knowledgeable.

I would definitely recommend you to come to the studio if you are looking for yoga classes in this area.

Fantastic miniature railway with a mix of steam and diesel trains. Two separate tracks, each with a double loop mean you get a great amount of time each ride. There is a great coffee / cake van there too, with benches and picnic area for lots of options.

Good fun for young kids (note: babes in arms can't tide trains).  A variety of different trains to ride on and, when we visited, an ice cream van and a food and coffee van.  Tickets cover the whole session and allow as many trips as your kids want.  All the staff very friendly and helpful, much waving at and from the trains.  Relax in the little grassy park and picnic if you want.  Parking is limited.
Great afternoon at the TDMR. We got soaked in the rain and managed to get on four of the five trains before it closed. Really impressed with the trains, tracks and how it's all organized.

Amazing place to have a great time, especially if your little one is crazy about trains like mine! They have the chance to ride miniature trains and all of them go crazy! A space for birthday parties is a green field that can host several parties at the same time. The kids run around, play and love absolutely everything! Such a great surprise!

reviews.text: If you are running an organised camp, then Woodlarks is the place to go. Great facilities for special needs, good camping facilities with onsite tents, showers, and washrooms. The cookhouse is well equipped, and the online management is brilliant. There is a fantastic outdoor heated pool and woodland walk.

I recently went camp at woodlarks. Very very nice grounds, some of the best.
Great activities all day, ranging from team building to archery and everything between.
The entire place was spotless with the help of bins located everywhere in plain sight but not an eye sore.
The staff were very knowledgeable, funny and helpful. The only thing I’d change is that there should always be a member of staff available throughout the night. It was harder to deal with things at night with no staff around.

Woodlarks Camp Site is, firstly a beautiful place for camping activities. It is situated in a green piece of land. Some of the trees here are over 75 years old. There are tents on site and you can also take your tents along if you wish. There are 5 stars facilities for disabled persons, so rest your mind if there are special needs as the staff in Woodlarks are specially trained and equipped physically, mentally and emotionally to make camping of great pleasure to people with special needs. Nick, Sarah and their team members are super fantastic. We went with a group of students who like to visit Woodlarks every year. And it's an experience I really like even though it was my first ever camping. I like to come back for sure. By the way, Woodlarks is run as a charity so only of their staff is paid. The rest find the place as their life and service to our communities. Bravo to these great team! 👊🏾👊🏾👊🏾

Magical place run by wonderful people. Woodlarks is so special. Went there in December with a group of students with special needs and the Christmas installation was just amazing. So much effort was made to make us feel welcome and comfortable. The Santa grotto and Xmas installations were beautiful.
Thank you for having us Nick and Sarah.
Thank you to all the volunteers!
Woodlarks is a wonderful place where people with all kinds of disabilities can have a camping holiday made possible. I love it.

Well worth considering.

My family and I have attended the priory for many years. The staff are amazing and the ambience is top draw. My son loves this place more than life and that speaks volumes if he's prepared to lay down the joystick.

A marvellous stables. With welcoming staff and lovely ponies Tandridge exceeds in terms of prices as we all know horse riding is very expensive hobby. On the occasion of being bitten and bucked off I highly recommend the large beast that is Flint!

An absolute joy to be here today.  Been to many a sanctuary but never one in the middle of a city.  Obviously won't be the largest thing you'll ever be to but the amount of aww-ness is off the scale - pigs, llamas, sheep, goats, chickens, guinea pigs, chickens, rabbits...anything else I can't think off-hand.  The staff seem very kind and the cafe was an absolute beauty, wish I had the time to just sit there and read my book and watch the ducks play about.  Will most definitely go back again.

Nice to have an animal farm in the hub of the city, suitable place for family with kids! However, the ice cream we bought here was the worse experience we had, with the very bad quality of the cookie con,  costed £3, very disappointing!!!

This place was a pleasant surprise while I was casually walking around and getting “lost”.  Loved making a donation in return for animal feed. There are handwashing stations throughout the farm so A+!

I just love to see animals that are obviously well cared for 😊

Great support from management and especially Dre (only started working 2 days ago) and Cat who accommodated for us so well (being a group supporting vulnerable adults too). So grateful for the experience and all the staff!

reviews.text: My Dad use to bring me & my brother when we was little, he then would take my daughter then he would take her two children. Sadly he has passed now, but me & mum continue to bring the youngest it is a special place for us great memories. Always friendly people & the Christmas lights were equally as wonderful.

Such a brilliant little place! Perfect for my train obsessed 4 year old and my 9month old loved tagging along too. We went on it three times in a row as he would’ve happily stayed on it all day. Lovely little setting and people were very friendly. Will definitely be going back

I have been to many such centers and though the main purpose is a garden centre with restaurant the miniature railway is brilliant. Never been to a better similar attraction. Good value for money AND they also spend some if their income on supporting local charities. Also run occasional days especially for disabled support organisations. Runs every weekend and midweek during school holidays. Look up East Herts Miniature Railway for information.

Underpriced! Only £1.50!?

An amazing little gem in east Herts. We visited on Sat 14 September. It was busy but that only added to the experience for our 1 year old. We went on three times, and there were three different trains running. Very professionally run, clear safety protocols in place, and a fun couple of hours for us. Choo choo!

On a trip back home we decided to make a detour... the East Herts Miniature Railway is located in the rather large Van Hage Garden Centre. It takes a bit of navigating to get through the garden centre out to where the railway is! There is a little ticket office where you can buy tickets (card thankfully accepted!)

The railway itself has been set up really nicely, a trip through a tunnel and a ride over a pond included! The volunteers were great and friendly with the kids, and the steam train did a great job getting us round the track! It was raining on our visit so we got a little wet, but the station area where you get on etc. was nice and dry.

A really great miniature railway, and for the kids (and me!) it made the visit to a garden centre worthwhile!

result.formatted_address: Buckingham Palace Rd, London SW1W 0QH, UK
result.name: The Royal Mews, Buckingham Palace

reviews.text:
We recently visited The Royal Mews at Buckingham Palace, and it was a truly memorable experience. It felt incredibly special to be able to see the magnificent royal horses and the stunning historic carriages up close — especially the iconic Gold State Coach used for coronations.

There’s something quite magical about being so close to such an important part of royal tradition and history. My child and I were both fascinated and genuinely impressed.

The staff were absolutely wonderful — warm, friendly, and always happy to answer questions or offer guidance. It was a lovely day out, both educational and inspiring. Highly recommend for anyone with an interest in the British Royal Family or heritage in general.

This is an amazing Carriage house around the corner from the entrance and exit to Buckingham Palace. Such a treat to see carriages that have carried kings and queens on special occasions. There were also stalls with horses and information to be learned about the staff on hand (who all live upstairs for generations!). Amazing and so worth the cost. You can walk around as long as you like. Kids are welcomed too! Take as many pictures as you like!!!

Saw some magnificent carriages here. Absolutely love the black ones (The Diamond Jubilee State Coach, Semi-State Landau, Miniature Landau, Donkey Barouche) and the Gold State Coach. Not crowded as well. To me, this place is so better than the palace itself.

Bought a ticket in advance so only had to queue for a while to get in soon after our allocated time. You need to go through security so try to travel light. Carriages were good to see and worth seeing if going to the palaces at the same time but I would not make a trip just to see them as you’re in and out in an hour. The golden coach is spectacular

highly recommend come to visit!
So many small details hidden and you will feel incredible to knowing how these kinds of royal carriages using in the past or even right now!

if you buy the royal day out package, will include Royal Mews, Kings Gallery, and Buckingham palace for a better price

They sell single rides or 4 rides for 5.00

It is a fun place to experience ✨️ for old and young there's a dog friendly cafe not far from the mini railway about 3mins to walk if that

Went there a month ago and today and plan on going every month as my 1 yo loves it. The staff are always super friendly and the trains are very cool and well maintained. The scenery is also very beautiful especially for younger kids. Thank you for everything we will be back

The venue is superbly kept and the club is open regularly every month for public rides , as well as occasional special holiday events.

Small children love riding on the trains as they wind through the woods, on the look-out for elves and fairies - I'm sure they must live here, as you can see their front doors!

Went on a bank holiday Sunday. Que was short and waited about 10 minutes. Lovely train ride for a cheap price plus play areas x2, free parking. Kids had a great time. Easily spend a 2 to 3  hours including a picnic.

Great fun for kids, but also for adults. Even though one locomotive broke down, the guys immediately provided a new train. During the ride, the operator explained that the train had been checked in the morning and everything was fine.
I definitely recommend it and next time I'm in England I'll come here too. Great train and great experiences!
Greetings to the entire team that creates Pinewood Miniature Railway!

result.formatted_address: Aldenham Rd, Radlett, Borehamwood WD6 3BA, UK
result.name: Aldenham Country Park

reviews.text:
I’ve been coming to this park since I was little, and it used to be one of my favourite places – peaceful, full of open space, and a perfect spot for family walks, playing, or just relaxing. It had that quiet charm and a real sense of community.

Lately though, it’s definitely changed. Some of the natural feel is gone – more concrete, fewer trees, and it can get a bit crowded or noisy depending on when you go. Don’t get me wrong, it’s still a good place to walk and bring the dog, but it just doesn’t have that same calm vibe it used to.
Parking is extortionate if there for less than a few hours. 5.50 regardless of how long or short your stay is. Reservoir is nice to walk/run around. Went for a park run so can't comment on the farm.

We visited for a day trip to the farm and their 100 Aker wood walk. The farm is clean and nicely spaced out. The animals were clearly well fed and looked after well. One of our highlights was the smiling goat! My 4 year old soon was amazed and loved visiting the houses of Eeyore, pooh and the others. He was a exciting walk from one house to the next with cute little stories and the trial book made it a little more fun. He left a letter for pooh and is hoping he will write back as he wasn't home when he visited. Would recommend a day trip here and would likely return. The cafe was reasonably priced and the food was great. The even make home made chips. The staff were all friendly and welcoming across the site as well.

Lovely area with great activities all around. However, we stayed in the camping which had absolutely no value for money. It’s suppose to be family friendly but there’s loud music and parties most evenings, also the facilities are way below expected quality and always dirty. Also, the grounds are filled with stinging weeds that can easily be plucked with a little bit of effort. Camping site is not recommend.

Lovely place to visit not too expensive.
Good selection of farm animals, which you are able to feed.
Seasonal events throught out the year.
Also has lovely scenic walks which you do not need to pay for (just pay for parking).
100 aker wood is a lovely walk but needs a bit of maintenance and to make more attractive and appealing.

My 11yr old Grandson has been to Stubbers with his school, he had a fantastic time and thoroughly enjoyed his mini adventure break, based on the Ockendon Road, Upminster. It is an expansive site with a very large Lake. Parking was simple with two large car parks.
He has participated in a  whole host of activities including climbing, laser tag, water sports like paddle boarding and banana boat.

He has had an experience that I’m sure will stay with him forever.
Thank you Oasis Academy Pinewood and thank you to the staff of Stubbers👍

My child attended a residential trip with his school. I was able to visit prior to the trip and found everything really well set out and activities available for all age ranges. You need to prebook activities though there are some you can book on the day.
The timetable for residential stays is great, allowing time for children to get involved and really enjoy themselves whilst enhancing both social and teamwork skills. There's a disco and a good menu.
As my child has additional needs, I travelled to collect and deliver them back meaning I needed to come after closing. Staff are very friendly and helpful on all levels and whilst this is quite a journey for us to travel, it's very reasonably priced and a great day out, outside of a residential trip.

Nice place for a get together. Fun evening spent doing archery. We had booked a 10 ppl group booking and it was a 45 minute slot. Time went by very quickly. may be will book a little longer one next time. Covered picnic huts and lot of play equipment kept the kids and adults busy.

Great place. Gets the kids away from screens and outside. Just the general admission is worth the visit with loads of reasonably priced adventure activities to mix in. Book during the holidays to avoid missing out. Super friendly staff and instructors, plus the little café sells great coffee.

This is one of our absolute favourite places to be, especially in the spring/summer months. The staff are incredibly welcoming and helpful, the activities are second to none and the facilities are fantastic. I would give 10 stars if I could!

We have our own slip of ancient woodland as well as all acres of land to play on. If your child has a disability, then ELHAP is the place to come and play!
This is a wonderful charity and my daughter loves her days there.

if you want a place that is FUN !! yet respectful of difference this is it.

reviews.text:
My wife is due today with our second baby. Our 1 1/2 year old boy was sleeping in the stroller (it was his sleeping time).
The receptionist didn't let my pregnant wife in for the appointment with the midwife. Saying that stroller is not allowed... Excuse me, but she is due today with a big belly, our boy is sleeping in the stroller and there is the appointment...
They supposed to support families and not let them down...
So angry and disappointed of Ealing Log Cabin services...
Unbelievable how much stress they causing :(

I’m writing a review now as I’ve stayed up lating Googling to see what has become of Log Cabin. My twin sister and I went to Log Cabin in my primary school years, around 2007-2012, and I see a lot has changed since it’s now 2024. When I went there, it was just one building that was a big hall (actually made out of logs), and a little blue-painted art block next to it ran by Kalpana. And that was it, if I remember correctly. It is a key happy memory from my childhood: Kalpana would help us make Diwali pots out of clay, and there was a huge wooden climbing frame with ramps; we would jump off the top level (all supervised, of course), and crawl under the lowest part of the ramp. There was netting underneath it and a big swing (shaped like a sack) at the back that was like a zip wire. This was before Ofsted inspections led to the Log Cabin becoming more of a secure and modern unit for children, rather that the rowdy outdoor climbing and adventure playground it used to be. I remember playing in the sandpit and the wendy house; and they had an awesome tyre swing that swung between two wooden platforms, which was then replaced by a cross-shaped contraption (4 swings that went up and down as well as horizontally). As Log Cabin got redeveloped, they added a sensory room and an indoor softplay. I can’t find any photos online of the old Log Cabin, sadly. The idea of mixing mainstream kids with children with learning difficulties was excellent, and we learnt to mix and play with these children as if they were no different. When our mum arrived we would beg her to let us stay and play for longer.  When my sister and I were there, the staff were Sam, Sara, Kalpana, David, Poonam and Dennis (the Mennis), and that’s all I can remember. Hope they’re all doing well.

This charity rents its venue for organisations/events, but they are far from any professionalism. They charge the premium price versus other venues around in Northfields. Not recommending hiring their place for any event. AVOID.

Log Cabin is a very special place which services the community, children and families. There are very sincere and committed people working here and i have seen the log cabin develop over the years, its remarkable as a lot of services have been cut due to the governments lack of understanding. I had to chase up my non verbal daughters head injury she picked up there for weeks and left numerous messages and nobody ever got back to me so she didn’t go back due to this. I even asked the SW at school to contact you guys regarding her injury but you didn’t respond to her email either. The communication is poor and there was more than one occasion that the Log Cabin have done exactly what I have asked them NOT to do. You should not be looking after children with severe needs if you can not ensure their safety, like your OFSTED report says. By our own experience at Log Cabin, I would say the OFSTED report is more than fair. You compromised my daughters safety more than once and then couldn’t be bothered to get back to us. Quite shocking. Hopefully there can be a huge improvement for all the other children who go there still.

reviews.text: My children, aged 7 and 9 (a boy and a girl); have been going to Timbuktu for the past year. They absolutely love going there. It is one of the few activities they do which always gets a thumbs up. In the holidays they can go every day and I keep expecting them to say they want to do something different but they keep wanting to go every day!! Part of that is the exciting activities planned each day, like Easter egg hunting, slime making, go-kart making, the disco. There is a big outdoor play area, with sand and water play, swings, slide and climbing frames . It is absolutely fantastic for them to go there in the evening, where they get lots of exercise and social interaction, compared to sitting at home on their phones or watching telly. They would even rather go there than the park with me because their friends are there and there are more activities. The staff are absolutely lovely, caring people who I feel completely confident to trust my children's well being with.  I feel so lucky to have Timbuktu nearby as it provides everything children need for healthy physical, emotional, social  and even brain  development.    This is especially needed in today's environment of fear about letting children play outside by themselves with their friends. Here they can play with their friends in a safe and stimulating environment. Brilliant!

My son  and I attend the Saturday family days on a regular basis, it is a great friendly environment with so much to do from amazing crafts, activities inside and lets not forget the amazing playground. There is so much to do we stay there from start to finish. The staff  there are so helpful, amazing and involve everyone in all activities.

The best thing about Timbuktu is how children can explore and learn in a safe place and how the centre has a massive community feel which is entirely child lead. my only regret about Timbuktu is not finding it sooner.

All the staff are amazing,so welcoming,friendly and caring for each child's needs. Healthy lunches given and plenty to drink to keep them hydrated. reviews.text: The One O Clock Club and Adventure Playground are two of the best things about living in this part of London. Your children can run wild with no shoes, get wonderfully wet and grubby and generally have a bit of a 90s childhood experience. There a thousand different toys to play and experiment.
